Fungal infection.What is the disease?: Fungal infections affect skin, nails, or mucosa due to fungal overgrowth.
Fungal infection.What are the symptoms?: Itching, rash, scaling, nail changes, discharge.
Fungal infection.What causes the disease?: Fungal organisms in warm, moist environments or reduced immunity.
Fungal infection.Prevention: Keep areas dry, good hygiene, avoid sharing personal items.
Fungal infection.Food: Use a balanced diet with enough protein; limit excess sugar if you are prone to recurrent fungal infections.
Fungal infection.How to control it?: Topical or oral antifungals as prescribed; keep area clean.
Fungal infection.When to see a doctor?: If spreading, involves nails, or does not improve.

Allergy.What is the disease?: Immune reaction to allergens like pollen, dust, foods, or medicines.
Allergy.What are the symptoms?: Sneezing, itchy eyes, rash, swelling, breathing difficulty in severe cases.
Allergy.What causes the disease?: Exposure to allergens that trigger the immune system.
Allergy.Prevention: Avoid triggers, use air filters, maintain hygiene.
Allergy.Food: Avoid known food allergens; choose simple home-cooked meals and stay well hydrated.
Allergy.How to control it?: Antihistamines, nasal sprays, avoid triggers; seek testing if persistent.
Allergy.When to see a doctor?: If breathing difficulty or severe symptoms occur.

GERD.What is the disease?: Acid reflux causing heartburn and regurgitation.
GERD.What are the symptoms?: Heartburn, sour taste, chest discomfort, regurgitation.
GERD.What causes the disease?: Stomach acid moves back into the esophagus.
GERD.Prevention: Avoid trigger foods, eat smaller meals, remain upright after eating.
GERD.Food: Prefer bland, low-fat foods such as oatmeal, banana, rice, yogurt, and avoid spicy, oily, or acidic foods.
GERD.How to control it?: Lifestyle changes, antacids, or acid-suppressing medicines.
GERD.When to see a doctor?: If persistent symptoms or difficulty swallowing.

Drug Reaction.What is the disease?: Adverse response to medication which can be mild or severe.
Drug Reaction.What causes the disease?: Sensitivity or allergy to a medicine.
Drug Reaction.Prevention: Inform clinicians of prior reactions; monitor new drugs.
Drug Reaction.Food: Drink water and take light meals if nauseated; avoid alcohol while recovering.
Drug Reaction.How to control it?: Stop offending drug, seek medical care; use emergency services for anaphylaxis.
Drug Reaction.When to see a doctor?: Immediately for breathing difficulty or swelling.

Peptic ulcer disease.What is the disease?: Sores in stomach or duodenum from acid damage.
Peptic ulcer disease.What are the symptoms?: Burning abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting blood, black stools.
Peptic ulcer disease.What causes the disease?: H. pylori infection, NSAIDs, smoking, or acid injury.
Peptic ulcer disease.Prevention: Avoid NSAID overuse, treat H. pylori when present.
Peptic ulcer disease.Food: Choose soft, non-spicy foods such as rice, toast, bananas, and avoid alcohol, coffee, and fried foods.
Peptic ulcer disease.How to control it?: Acid suppression and antibiotics if needed.
Peptic ulcer disease.When to see a doctor?: If severe pain, vomiting blood, or black stools.

AIDS.What is the disease?: Advanced HIV infection causing severe immune compromise.
AIDS.What are the symptoms?: Weight loss, recurrent infections, chronic diarrhea.
AIDS.Prevention: Safe sex, clean needles, testing and treatment.
AIDS.Food: Eat a high-protein, calorie-adequate diet with fruits, vegetables, whole grains, and safe cooked foods.
AIDS.How to control it?: Antiretroviral therapy and prevention of opportunistic infections.
AIDS.When to see a doctor?: For any new infections or weight loss.

Diabetes.What is the disease?: Metabolic disorder with high blood sugar.
Diabetes.What are the symptoms?: Thirst, frequent urination, fatigue, slow healing.
Diabetes.Food: Focus on high-fiber meals, vegetables, pulses, whole grains, lean protein, and limit sugary drinks and refined carbs.
Diabetes.How to control it?: Medication, insulin when needed, lifestyle management.
Diabetes.When to see a doctor?: If uncontrolled sugars or signs of complications.

Gastroenteritis.What is the disease?: Inflammation of stomach and intestines causing diarrhea and vomiting.
Gastroenteritis.What causes the disease?: Infection from contaminated food or water.
Gastroenteritis.Prevention: Hand hygiene, safe food and water.
Gastroenteritis.Food: Use oral rehydration solution, rice gruel, banana, toast, and clear soups; avoid oily, spicy, and heavy foods.
Gastroenteritis.How to control it?: Oral rehydration, rest; seek care for severe dehydration.
Gastroenteritis.When to see a doctor?: If persistent high fever, bloody stools, or dehydration.

Bronchial Asthma.What is the disease?: Chronic airway disease causing wheeze and breathlessness.
Bronchial Asthma.What causes the disease?: Triggers such as allergens, infections, exercise, or pollution.
Bronchial Asthma.Food: No special diet is required; eat light balanced meals and avoid foods that you know trigger symptoms.
Bronchial Asthma.How to control it?: Inhaled bronchodilators and steroids; emergency care for severe attacks.
Bronchial Asthma.When to see a doctor?: If increasing inhaler use or worsening symptoms.

Hypertension.What is the disease?: Persistent high blood pressure increasing cardiovascular risk.
Hypertension.What are the symptoms?: Often none; may cause headache when very high.
Hypertension.What causes the disease?: Genetics, salt intake, obesity, inactivity, or other medical causes.
Hypertension.Food: Use a DASH-style diet with vegetables, fruits, legumes, whole grains, and low-salt cooking.

Migraine.What is the disease?: Recurrent severe headaches often with nausea and light sensitivity.
Migraine.What causes the disease?: Triggers like stress, sleep changes, hormones, or certain foods.
Migraine.Food: Eat regular meals, stay hydrated, and avoid common triggers like skipped meals, excess caffeine, aged cheese, or alcohol.
Migraine.How to control it?: Early analgesics or triptans; preventive drugs for frequent attacks.
Migraine.When to see a doctor?: If pattern changes or neurological signs appear.

Jaundice.What is the disease?: Yellowing of skin/eyes due to liver or blood disorders.
Jaundice.What are the symptoms?: Yellow skin/eyes, dark urine, pale stools.
Jaundice.What causes the disease?: Liver disease, bile blockage, or blood breakdown.
Jaundice.Prevention: Vaccination for viral hepatitis, avoid alcohol.
Jaundice.Food: Choose light, low-fat meals, drink water, and avoid alcohol and very oily foods.
Jaundice.When to see a doctor?: When yellowing appears or with severe pain/fever.

Malaria.What is the disease?: Parasitic infection transmitted by mosquitoes causing fever.
Malaria.What are the symptoms?: High fever, chills, headache, muscle pain.
Malaria.What causes the disease?: Plasmodium parasites spread by mosquito bites.
Malaria.Prevention: Bed nets, repellents, remove standing water.
Malaria.Food: Drink plenty of fluids and eat nourishing soft foods like rice, dal, soups, fruits, and eggs if tolerated.

Dengue.What is the disease?: Viral infection from Aedes mosquitoes causing high fever and pain.
Dengue.What are the symptoms?: High fever, severe headache, joint pain, rash.
Dengue.What causes the disease?: Dengue virus spread by mosquito bites.
Dengue.Food: Hydrate well with water, ORS, coconut water, soups, and fruit juices; avoid oily and heavy foods.
Dengue.How to control it?: Supportive care; monitor for warning signs.
Dengue.When to see a doctor?: If bleeding or severe abdominal pain occurs.

Pneumonia.What is the disease?: Infection of the lungs causing cough and breathlessness.
Pneumonia.What are the symptoms?: Cough with phlegm, fever, chest pain, breathlessness.
Pneumonia.Food: Take warm fluids, soups, soft protein-rich foods, and plenty of water if swallowing is safe.
Pneumonia.How to control it?: Medical assessment; antibiotics for bacterial causes.
Pneumonia.When to see a doctor?: If shortness of breath or high fever.

Tuberculosis.What is the disease?: Bacterial lung infection treatable with long-course antibiotics.
Tuberculosis.What are the symptoms?: Chronic cough, weight loss, night sweats, fever.
Tuberculosis.What causes the disease?: Mycobacterium tuberculosis spread through air droplets.
Tuberculosis.Prevention: BCG where used, good ventilation, early treatment.
Tuberculosis.Food: Eat a high-protein, calorie-adequate diet with eggs, pulses, milk, vegetables, fruits, and whole grains.
Tuberculosis.When to see a doctor?: If cough >2 weeks or weight loss.

Typhoid.What is the disease?: Bacterial infection causing prolonged fever and abdominal symptoms.
Typhoid.What are the symptoms?: High fever, abdominal pain, constipation or diarrhea, headache.
Typhoid.What causes the disease?: Salmonella typhi from contaminated food or water.
Typhoid.Prevention: Safe water and food practices; vaccination when indicated.
Typhoid.Food: Use boiled water, soft bland foods, soups, and avoid street food, raw salads, and unpasteurized products during illness.
Typhoid.When to see a doctor?: If high fever or severe abdominal pain.

Influenza.What is the disease?: Viral respiratory illness causing fever and body aches.
Influenza.What are the symptoms?: Fever, cough, sore throat, body aches.
Influenza.Food: Drink warm fluids, soups, and eat easy-to-digest foods like rice, porridge, banana, and toast.
Influenza.How to control it?: Supportive care; antivirals early when indicated.
Influenza.When to see a doctor?: If breathing difficulty or severe symptoms.

Conjunctivitis.What is the disease?: Inflammation of the eye lining causing redness and discharge.
Conjunctivitis.What causes the disease?: Viral, bacterial, allergic, or irritant causes.
Conjunctivitis.Food: No special food is needed; maintain hydration and eat a balanced diet to support recovery.
Conjunctivitis.How to control it?: Keep eyes clean; use prescribed drops if bacterial.
Conjunctivitis.When to see a doctor?: If vision worsens or severe pain.

Urinary Tract Infection.What is the disease?: Infection of urinary tract causing burning and frequency.
Urinary Tract Infection.What are the symptoms?: Burning on urination, frequent urges, cloudy urine.
Urinary Tract Infection.Food: Drink plenty of water; cranberry products may help some people, and avoid excess caffeine and alcohol.
Urinary Tract Infection.When to see a doctor?: If fever, flank pain, or blood in urine.

Kidney stones.What is the disease?: Hard mineral deposits in kidneys causing severe pain.
Kidney stones.What are the symptoms?: Severe flank pain, blood in urine, nausea.
Kidney stones.Food: Drink plenty of water, and limit excess salt, cola drinks, and very high-oxalate foods if advised by a clinician.
Kidney stones.How to control it?: Pain control, hydration, medical or surgical treatment.
Kidney stones.When to see a doctor?: If severe pain, fever, or inability to pass urine.

Hepatitis A.What is the disease?: Viral liver infection spread via contaminated food/water.
Hepatitis A.What causes the disease?: Hepatitis A virus from contaminated food or water.
Hepatitis A.Food: Use easy-to-digest foods, fresh fruit, cooked vegetables, and avoid alcohol and heavy fried foods.

Hepatitis B.What is the disease?: Viral infection affecting the liver; may become chronic.
Hepatitis B.What causes the disease?: Hepatitis B virus transmitted by blood or body fluids.
Hepatitis B.Food: Eat regular balanced meals, stay hydrated, and avoid alcohol.
Hepatitis B.How to control it?: Monitor and antiviral therapy for chronic cases.

Chronic Kidney Disease.What is the disease?: Gradual loss of kidney function over time.
Chronic Kidney Disease.What causes the disease?: Often diabetes, hypertension, or other chronic kidney damage.
Chronic Kidney Disease.Food: Follow a kidney-friendly diet with controlled salt, protein, and potassium as advised by a clinician or dietitian.
Chronic Kidney Disease.How to control it?: Manage causes, specialist care, dialysis in advanced stages.
Chronic Kidney Disease.When to see a doctor?: If swelling, breathlessness, or abnormal tests.

COPD.What is the disease?: Chronic lung disease causing airflow limitation and breathlessness.
COPD.What causes the disease?: Usually long-term smoking or pollutant exposure.
COPD.Food: Eat small frequent meals with enough protein and calories; warm fluids can help if coughing is bothersome.
COPD.How to control it?: Inhalers, pulmonary rehabilitation, oxygen if needed.

Coronary Artery Disease.What is the disease?: Narrowing of heart arteries reducing blood flow to heart.
Coronary Artery Disease.What causes the disease?: Atherosclerosis from high cholesterol, smoking, diabetes, or hypertension.
Coronary Artery Disease.Food: Choose heart-healthy foods like vegetables, fruits, oats, pulses, fish, and limit fried foods, trans fats, and excess salt.
Coronary Artery Disease.How to control it?: Medications, angioplasty, or bypass if indicated.
Coronary Artery Disease.When to see a doctor?: If chest pain or fainting episodes.

Heart Failure.What is the disease?: Condition where heart cannot pump effectively causing fluid buildup.
Heart Failure.What causes the disease?: Heart attack, hypertension, valve disease, or cardiomyopathy.
Heart Failure.Prevention: Control heart conditions and risk factors.
Heart Failure.Food: Follow a low-salt diet, limit packaged foods, and keep fluid intake as advised by the doctor.
Heart Failure.When to see a doctor?: If sudden weight gain or worsening breathlessness.

Stroke.What is the disease?: Sudden brain function loss due to blocked or burst vessels.
Stroke.What are the symptoms?: Weakness on one side, slurred speech, facial droop.
Stroke.What causes the disease?: Blocked blood vessel or bleeding in the brain.
Stroke.Prevention: Control blood pressure, diabetes, stop smoking.
Stroke.Food: After recovery, use a heart-healthy low-salt diet with vegetables, fruits, whole grains, and lean proteins.
Stroke.When to see a doctor?: Immediately at any sign of stroke.

Anemia.What is the disease?: Low red blood cells or hemoglobin causing fatigue and pallor.
Anemia.What causes the disease?: Iron deficiency, vitamin deficiency, chronic disease, or blood loss.
Anemia.Prevention: Adequate nutrition and treat bleeding sources.
Anemia.Food: Eat iron-rich foods such as leafy greens, beans, lentils, eggs, meat, and vitamin-C-rich fruits to help absorption.
Anemia.How to control it?: Iron or other supplements and treat underlying cause.
Anemia.When to see a doctor?: If persistent fatigue or signs of bleeding.

Hypothyroidism.What is the disease?: Underactive thyroid causing fatigue and weight gain.
Hypothyroidism.What causes the disease?: Autoimmune disease, iodine deficiency, or thyroid surgery.
Hypothyroidism.Prevention: Early diagnosis; treat iodine deficiency where present.
Hypothyroidism.Food: Use a balanced diet; if iodine is lacking, include iodine-rich foods only as advised by a clinician.
Hypothyroidism.When to see a doctor?: If persistent fatigue or weight changes.

Hyperthyroidism.What is the disease?: Overactive thyroid causing weight loss and palpitations.
Hyperthyroidism.What causes the disease?: Graves' disease, nodules, or thyroid inflammation.
Hyperthyroidism.Food: Eat enough calories and protein through regular meals; avoid excess caffeine if palpitations are present.

Eczema.What is the disease?: Chronic skin inflammation causing dry, itchy patches.
Eczema.What are the symptoms?: Itching, dryness, redness, oozing in flares.
Eczema.What causes the disease?: Skin barrier problems and triggers such as irritants or allergies.
Eczema.Food: No specific diet is required, but a balanced diet and adequate water intake support skin health.
Eczema.How to control it?: Emollients and topical steroids for flares.

Psoriasis.What is the disease?: Autoimmune skin disease causing scaly plaques.
Psoriasis.What are the symptoms?: Scaly red patches, itching, nail changes.
Psoriasis.Food: A balanced anti-inflammatory pattern is reasonable: vegetables, fruits, whole grains, fish, and less alcohol and fried food.

Acne.What is the disease?: Common skin condition with pimples and blackheads.
Acne.What causes the disease?: Oil, blocked pores, bacteria, and hormones.
Acne.Food: Choose a balanced diet, drink water, and if breakouts worsen with certain foods, reduce sugary drinks and high-glycemic snacks.
Acne.How to control it?: Topical treatments, oral meds for severe cases.
Acne.When to see a doctor?: If cystic acne or scarring occurs.

Bronchitis.What is the disease?: Inflammation of bronchial tubes causing cough and sputum.
Bronchitis.What causes the disease?: Usually viral infection or smoking-related irritation.
Bronchitis.Food: Warm fluids, soups, and fruits can soothe the throat and help hydration.

Cellulitis.What is the disease?: Bacterial skin infection causing warmth, redness, and swelling.
Cellulitis.What causes the disease?: Bacteria entering through a wound or skin break.
Cellulitis.Food: Eat normal balanced meals and keep well hydrated to support healing.
Cellulitis.When to see a doctor?: If redness spreads or fever develops.

Appendicitis.What is the disease?: Inflammation of appendix often requiring surgical removal.
Appendicitis.What are the symptoms?: Severe localized abdominal pain, nausea, fever.
Appendicitis.What causes the disease?: Blockage and inflammation of the appendix.
Appendicitis.Prevention: No reliable prevention; seek early care for severe pain.
Appendicitis.Food: Do not force food if pain is severe; avoid heavy meals and follow urgent medical advice.

Sepsis.What is the disease?: Life-threatening organ dysfunction from severe infection.
Sepsis.What are the symptoms?: Fever or low temperature, fast heart rate, confusion.
Sepsis.What causes the disease?: Severe infection spreading through the body.
Sepsis.Food: If awake and able to swallow, sip water only until urgent medical review; do not delay treatment for eating.
Sepsis.How to control it?: Immediate hospital care with antibiotics and support.
Sepsis.When to see a doctor?: Immediately for signs of severe infection.

Otitis Media.What is the disease?: Middle ear infection causing ear pain and fever.
Otitis Media.What causes the disease?: Infection behind the eardrum, often after a cold.
Otitis Media.Food: No special diet is needed; warm fluids and regular meals are fine.
Otitis Media.When to see a doctor?: If severe pain, high fever, or drainage.

Sinusitis.What is the disease?: Inflammation of sinuses causing facial pain and congestion.
Sinusitis.What are the symptoms?: Facial pain, nasal congestion, thick discharge.
Sinusitis.What causes the disease?: Usually a viral infection, sometimes bacterial.
Sinusitis.Food: Warm fluids and soups can help; avoid dehydration.
Sinusitis.How to control it?: Nasal saline, decongestants, antibiotics if bacterial.
Sinusitis.When to see a doctor?: If severe pain, fever, or symptoms >10 days.

Tonsillitis.What is the disease?: Inflammation of tonsils causing sore throat and fever.
Tonsillitis.What are the symptoms?: Sore throat, swollen tonsils, difficulty swallowing.
Tonsillitis.Food: Choose soft foods like soups, porridge, yogurt, and warm fluids to reduce throat pain.
Tonsillitis.How to control it?: Analgesics, antibiotics if bacterial; ENT follow-up if recurrent.
Tonsillitis.When to see a doctor?: If drooling, severe pain, or breathing difficulty.

Meningitis.What is the disease?: Inflammation of brain/spinal cord membranes often severe.
Meningitis.What are the symptoms?: Severe headache, neck stiffness, fever, confusion.
Meningitis.What causes the disease?: Bacterial, viral, or other infections affecting the membranes around the brain and spinal cord.
Meningitis.Prevention: Vaccination where available; early infection treatment.
Meningitis.Food: If symptoms are suspected, do not rely on food remedies; seek urgent care immediately.
Meningitis.How to control it?: Immediate hospital care and antibiotics for bacterial meningitis.
Meningitis.When to see a doctor?: Immediately for severe headache and neck stiffness.

Chickenpox.What is the disease?: Viral infection causing itchy vesicular rash and fever.
Chickenpox.What are the symptoms?: Fever and itchy vesicles that crust over.
Chickenpox.Prevention: Vaccination and avoid contact with infected persons.
Chickenpox.Food: Drink fluids and eat soft, cool foods if the mouth is sore; avoid spicy or acidic foods.
Chickenpox.How to control it?: Symptomatic care; antivirals in severe cases.
Chickenpox.When to see a doctor?: If severe fever, breathing problems, or in newborns.

Measles.What is the disease?: Highly contagious viral illness with fever and rash.
Measles.What are the symptoms?: Fever, cough, conjunctivitis, followed by rash.
Measles.Food: Use fluids, soups, and soft nourishing foods to maintain strength during fever.
Measles.When to see a doctor?: If breathing problems or severe symptoms.

Rubella.What is the disease?: Viral infection causing mild rash; serious in pregnancy.
Rubella.What are the symptoms?: Mild fever and rash, swollen glands.
Rubella.Food: Eat normally and stay hydrated; no special diet is needed.
Rubella.How to control it?: Supportive care; obstetric review if exposed in pregnancy.

Poliomyelitis.What is the disease?: Viral infection that can cause paralysis; prevented by vaccine.
Poliomyelitis.What are the symptoms?: Fever, fatigue, and in severe cases paralysis.
Poliomyelitis.Food: Maintain good nutrition and fluids; soft foods may help if swallowing is weak.
Poliomyelitis.How to control it?: Supportive care and rehabilitation for paralysis.

HPV infection.What is the disease?: Human papillomavirus infection; some types cause warts or cancer.
HPV infection.What are the symptoms?: Often asymptomatic; may cause warts or abnormal screening.
HPV infection.Prevention: HPV vaccination and safe sex practices.
HPV infection.Food: No special food is required; a balanced diet supports overall immune health.
HPV infection.How to control it?: Treat warts and follow-up for abnormal screening.
HPV infection.When to see a doctor?: If warts or abnormal bleeding occur.

Osteoarthritis.What is the disease?: Degenerative joint disease causing pain and stiffness.
Osteoarthritis.Prevention: Maintain healthy weight and joint care.
Osteoarthritis.Food: A balanced diet with weight control helps; prioritize vegetables, fruits, lean protein, and limit excess sugar and fried foods.
Osteoarthritis.How to control it?: Pain relief, physiotherapy, joint replacement if severe.

Arthritis.What is the disease?: Arthritis is inflammation of one or more joints, causing pain and stiffness that can worsen with age.
Arthritis.What are the symptoms?: Joint pain, swelling, stiffness (especially in the morning), and reduced range of motion.
Arthritis.What causes the disease?: Joint wear and tear, autoimmune conditions, infection, or crystal buildup (gout), depending on the type.
Arthritis.Prevention: Maintain a healthy weight, stay active with joint-friendly exercise, and avoid repetitive joint strain.
Arthritis.Food: Eat anti-inflammatory foods (fruits, vegetables, fish); limit processed and sugary foods.
Arthritis.How to control it?: Pain relievers, anti-inflammatory medicine, physiotherapy, and joint-protection techniques.
Arthritis.When to see a doctor?: See a doctor if joint swelling, redness, and pain are severe, sudden, or affect daily activities.

Heart Attack.What is the disease?: A heart attack (myocardial infarction) happens when blood flow to part of the heart muscle is suddenly blocked, usually by a clot in a coronary artery, damaging the heart tissue.
Heart Attack.What are the symptoms?: Chest pain or pressure, pain spreading to the arm, jaw, or back, shortness of breath, cold sweat, nausea, and lightheadedness.
Heart Attack.What causes the disease?: A blood clot blocking a coronary artery narrowed by fatty plaque (atherosclerosis), often linked to smoking, high blood pressure, high cholesterol, diabetes, and obesity.
Heart Attack.Prevention: Control blood pressure, cholesterol, and blood sugar; avoid smoking; exercise regularly; eat a heart-healthy diet.
Heart Attack.Food: Eat vegetables, fruits, whole grains, and lean protein; limit salt, saturated fat, and fried food.
Heart Attack.How to control it?: Emergency treatment (clot-busting drugs or angioplasty), followed by medicines like aspirin, statins, and blood pressure control, plus cardiac rehabilitation.
Heart Attack.When to see a doctor?: Call emergency services immediately for chest pain, breathlessness, or collapse -- do not wait or self-treat.

Vertigo.What is the disease?: Vertigo is a false sensation of spinning or movement, usually caused by a problem in the inner ear's balance system.
Vertigo.What are the symptoms?: A spinning sensation, loss of balance, nausea, vomiting, and unsteadiness, often triggered by head movement.
Vertigo.What causes the disease?: Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (displaced inner-ear crystals), inner ear infections, Meniere's disease, or migraine.
Vertigo.Prevention: Move the head slowly, avoid sudden position changes, and treat underlying ear conditions promptly.
Vertigo.Food: Stay well hydrated and limit salt and caffeine if Meniere's disease is suspected.
Vertigo.How to control it?: Head-repositioning exercises (like the Epley maneuver), vestibular rehabilitation, and medicines for nausea if needed.
Vertigo.When to see a doctor?: See a doctor if vertigo is severe, persistent, or accompanied by hearing loss, double vision, weakness, or slurred speech.

Cervical Spondylosis.What is the disease?: Cervical spondylosis is age-related wear and tear of the disks and joints in the neck (cervical spine).
Cervical Spondylosis.What are the symptoms?: Neck pain and stiffness, headaches, numbness or weakness in the arms, and reduced range of neck motion.
Cervical Spondylosis.What causes the disease?: Gradual disk dehydration, bone spurs, and ligament stiffening with age, worsened by poor posture or repetitive neck strain.
Cervical Spondylosis.Prevention: Maintain good posture, take breaks from prolonged screen or desk work, and do neck-strengthening exercises.
Cervical Spondylosis.Food: Eat a balanced diet with calcium and vitamin D to support bone and joint health.
Cervical Spondylosis.How to control it?: Pain relievers, physiotherapy, neck exercises, and in severe cases a cervical collar or surgery.
Cervical Spondylosis.When to see a doctor?: See a doctor if there is arm weakness, numbness, loss of bladder or bowel control, or worsening pain.

Chronic Cholestasis.What is the disease?: Chronic cholestasis is a long-term reduction or blockage of bile flow from the liver, causing bile to build up in the body.
Chronic Cholestasis.What are the symptoms?: Persistent itching, yellowing of skin and eyes (jaundice), dark urine, pale stools, and fatigue.
Chronic Cholestasis.What causes the disease?: Liver diseases such as primary biliary cholangitis, bile duct blockage (gallstones, strictures, tumors), or certain medicines.
Chronic Cholestasis.Prevention: Limit alcohol, avoid liver-toxic medicines without medical advice, and get regular checkups if you have liver disease.
Chronic Cholestasis.Food: Eat a low-fat, easily digestible diet; your doctor may recommend fat-soluble vitamin supplements (A, D, E, K).
Chronic Cholestasis.How to control it?: Treat the underlying cause, medicines to relieve itching and improve bile flow, and monitoring liver function.
Chronic Cholestasis.When to see a doctor?: See a doctor for persistent itching, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or pale stools and dark urine.

Common Cold.What is the disease?: The common cold is a mild viral infection of the nose and throat, usually caused by rhinoviruses.
Common Cold.What are the symptoms?: Runny or blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, mild cough, and sometimes low-grade fever.
Common Cold.What causes the disease?: Viral infection spread through droplets or contaminated surfaces, easily transmitted in close contact.
Common Cold.Prevention: Wash hands frequently, avoid close contact with sick people, and avoid touching the face with unwashed hands.
Common Cold.Food: Drink warm fluids, eat light nutritious food, and stay well hydrated.
Common Cold.How to control it?: Rest, fluids, steam inhalation, and over-the-counter medicine for symptom relief; antibiotics are not needed.
Common Cold.When to see a doctor?: See a doctor if fever is high, symptoms last more than 10 days, or breathing becomes difficult.

Dimorphic Hemorrhoids.What is the disease?: Dimorphic hemorrhoids (piles) are swollen veins in the lower rectum and anus, occurring both internally and externally.
Dimorphic Hemorrhoids.What are the symptoms?: Rectal bleeding, itching, pain, and a lump near the anus, especially during or after bowel movements.
Dimorphic Hemorrhoids.What causes the disease?: Straining during bowel movements, chronic constipation, prolonged sitting, pregnancy, or a low-fiber diet.
Dimorphic Hemorrhoids.Prevention: Eat a high-fiber diet, drink enough water, avoid straining, and avoid prolonged sitting on the toilet.
Dimorphic Hemorrhoids.Food: Eat fiber-rich foods like fruits, vegetables, and whole grains; drink plenty of water.
Dimorphic Hemorrhoids.How to control it?: Warm sitz baths, fiber supplements, topical creams; severe cases may need a minor procedure or surgery.
Dimorphic Hemorrhoids.When to see a doctor?: See a doctor for persistent bleeding, severe pain, or a lump that does not resolve.

Hypoglycemia.What is the disease?: Hypoglycemia is an abnormally low level of blood sugar (glucose), most common in people being treated for diabetes.
Hypoglycemia.What are the symptoms?: Shakiness, sweating, confusion, rapid heartbeat, hunger, dizziness, and in severe cases fainting or seizures.
Hypoglycemia.What causes the disease?: Too much diabetes medicine or insulin, skipped meals, excess exercise, or excess alcohol without food.
Hypoglycemia.Prevention: Eat meals on schedule, monitor blood sugar regularly, and adjust medicine doses with your doctor's guidance.
Hypoglycemia.Food: Keep a fast-acting sugar source (glucose tablets, juice) on hand; eat regular balanced meals.
Hypoglycemia.How to control it?: Take fast-acting sugar immediately (juice, glucose tablets); recheck blood sugar and seek help if it doesn't improve.
Hypoglycemia.When to see a doctor?: Seek urgent care for confusion, loss of consciousness, or seizures, or if low sugar episodes happen often.

Impetigo.What is the disease?: Impetigo is a common, highly contagious bacterial skin infection that causes red sores, often around the nose and mouth.
Impetigo.What are the symptoms?: Red sores that quickly rupture, ooze, and form a yellow-brown crust, usually itchy but not very painful.
Impetigo.What causes the disease?: Infection with Staphylococcus aureus or Streptococcus bacteria, entering through a break in the skin.
Impetigo.Prevention: Keep skin clean, avoid sharing towels or personal items, and treat cuts or insect bites promptly.
Impetigo.Food: No special diet; a balanced diet supports healing and immune health.
Impetigo.How to control it?: Topical or oral antibiotics as prescribed, keep the area clean, and avoid scratching.
Impetigo.When to see a doctor?: See a doctor if sores spread rapidly, don't improve with care, or fever develops.

Paralysis.What is the disease?: Paralysis is the loss of muscle function in part of the body, here linked to brain hemorrhage (bleeding inside the brain).
Paralysis.What are the symptoms?: Sudden weakness or loss of movement on one side of the body, slurred speech, facial drooping, and severe headache.
Paralysis.What causes the disease?: Bleeding into the brain from a ruptured blood vessel, often due to high blood pressure, aneurysm, or head injury.
Paralysis.Prevention: Control blood pressure, avoid smoking and excess alcohol, and treat conditions that raise bleeding risk.
Paralysis.Food: Low-salt, heart-healthy diet to help manage blood pressure; soft foods may be needed if swallowing is affected.
Paralysis.How to control it?: Emergency hospital treatment, followed by physiotherapy and rehabilitation to regain function.
Paralysis.When to see a doctor?: This is a medical emergency -- call emergency services immediately for sudden weakness, slurred speech, or severe headache.

Varicose Veins.What is the disease?: Varicose veins are swollen, twisted veins, usually in the legs, caused by weakened vein walls and faulty valves.
Varicose Veins.What are the symptoms?: Bulging, blue or purple veins, leg heaviness, aching, swelling, and itching around the affected veins.
Varicose Veins.What causes the disease?: Weak vein valves allowing blood to pool, worsened by prolonged standing, obesity, pregnancy, or aging.
Varicose Veins.Prevention: Avoid prolonged standing or sitting, exercise regularly, maintain healthy weight, and elevate legs when resting.
Varicose Veins.Food: Eat a high-fiber, low-salt diet to support circulation and avoid constipation-related straining.
Varicose Veins.How to control it?: Compression stockings, leg elevation, exercise; severe cases may need minimally invasive procedures.
Varicose Veins.When to see a doctor?: See a doctor if veins are painful, skin changes color, or an ulcer develops near the ankle.

Alcoholic Hepatitis.What is the disease?: Alcoholic hepatitis is liver inflammation caused by excessive alcohol consumption over time.
Alcoholic Hepatitis.What are the symptoms?: Jaundice, abdominal pain and swelling, fever, nausea, and loss of appetite.
Alcoholic Hepatitis.What causes the disease?: Heavy, prolonged alcohol use damaging liver cells and causing inflammation.
Alcoholic Hepatitis.Prevention: Limit or avoid alcohol, and seek help for alcohol dependence.
Alcoholic Hepatitis.Food: Eat a nutritious, protein-adequate diet as advised by a doctor; strictly avoid alcohol.
Alcoholic Hepatitis.How to control it?: Complete alcohol abstinence, nutritional support, and medical treatment for liver inflammation.
Alcoholic Hepatitis.When to see a doctor?: See a doctor urgently for jaundice, confusion, abdominal swelling, or vomiting blood.

Hepatitis C.What is the disease?: Hepatitis C is a liver infection caused by the hepatitis C virus, often becoming a chronic infection that can damage the liver over time.
Hepatitis C.What are the symptoms?: Often no early symptoms; when present -- fatigue, yellowing of skin and eyes, dark urine, and abdominal pain.
Hepatitis C.What causes the disease?: Spread mainly through contact with infected blood (unsafe injections, unscreened blood, shared needles).
Hepatitis C.Prevention: Avoid sharing needles, ensure safe blood screening, and use sterile medical or tattoo equipment.
Hepatitis C.Food: Eat a balanced, liver-friendly diet and avoid alcohol.
Hepatitis C.How to control it?: Antiviral medicines can cure most cases; regular liver function monitoring is important.
Hepatitis C.When to see a doctor?: See a doctor for jaundice, prolonged fatigue, or known exposure to the virus for testing.

Hepatitis D.What is the disease?: Hepatitis D is a liver infection caused by the hepatitis D virus, which only infects people already infected with hepatitis B.
Hepatitis D.What are the symptoms?: Fatigue, jaundice, abdominal pain, nausea, and dark urine, often more severe than hepatitis B alone.
Hepatitis D.What causes the disease?: Requires co-infection with hepatitis B; spreads through infected blood and body fluids.
Hepatitis D.Prevention: Hepatitis B vaccination prevents hepatitis D; avoid sharing needles and unsafe blood products.
Hepatitis D.Food: Liver-friendly diet, avoid alcohol, and maintain good nutrition.
Hepatitis D.How to control it?: Managed by treating hepatitis B; antiviral options are limited, so prevention is key.
Hepatitis D.When to see a doctor?: See a doctor promptly for jaundice or worsening liver symptoms, especially with known hepatitis B infection.

Hepatitis E.What is the disease?: Hepatitis E is a liver infection caused by the hepatitis E virus, usually spread through contaminated water.
Hepatitis E.What are the symptoms?: Fatigue, jaundice, nausea, abdominal pain, and dark urine; usually self-limiting.
Hepatitis E.What causes the disease?: Drinking water or food contaminated with the virus, common in areas with poor sanitation.
Hepatitis E.Prevention: Drink safe or boiled water, practice good hygiene, and ensure proper sanitation.
Hepatitis E.Food: Light, easily digestible, liver-friendly diet; avoid alcohol and stay hydrated.
Hepatitis E.How to control it?: Usually resolves with rest and supportive care; pregnant women need close monitoring as it can be severe.
Hepatitis E.When to see a doctor?: See a doctor for jaundice, especially in pregnancy, or if symptoms worsen.

Cancer (General).What is the disease?: Cancer is a condition in which some body cells grow in an uncontrolled way and can spread to nearby tissues or distant organs. In simple terms, the normal control system of the body fails in those cells. Cancer can start in almost any organ such as breast, lung, mouth, stomach, blood, or cervix. Some cancers grow slowly, while others become dangerous quickly. Early detection gives better treatment success. Many people can live long and productive lives with timely diagnosis, proper treatment, and regular follow-up care.
Cancer (General).What are the symptoms?: Symptoms vary by organ, but common warning signs include unexplained weight loss, long-lasting tiredness, a lump that does not go away, persistent cough, bleeding without clear reason, change in bowel or urine habits, non-healing mouth ulcer, unusual skin change, persistent pain, or repeated fever. In rural settings, people may ignore these as weakness or infection, but persistent symptoms need evaluation. Not every symptom means cancer, yet warning signs lasting more than two to three weeks should be checked by a qualified doctor for early diagnosis.
Cancer (General).What causes the disease?: Cancer usually develops due to a combination of causes: tobacco chewing or smoking, alcohol use, unhealthy diet, obesity, low physical activity, long-term infections (for example HPV, hepatitis B/C), family history, radiation exposure, and harmful chemicals. In some people, age and inherited genetic changes increase risk even without obvious external causes. Many cancers occur because cell DNA gets damaged over years. Avoiding tobacco, reducing alcohol, getting vaccines, and screening can reduce risk significantly, but even healthy people can still develop cancer, so warning symptoms must never be ignored.
Cancer (General).Stages: Stage 1: Cancer is small and has not spread. Stage 2: Cancer has grown but not spread much. Stage 3: Cancer has spread to nearby tissues. Stage 4: Cancer has spread to other organs (most serious).
Cancer (General).Prevention: Prevention focuses on reducing avoidable risks. Do not smoke or chew tobacco, avoid second-hand smoke, limit alcohol, eat vegetables, fruits, whole grains, and pulses, keep a healthy body weight, and stay physically active. Take vaccines like HPV and hepatitis B where advised. Practice safe sex and avoid unsafe injections. Use protective gear if exposed to dust or chemicals at work. Attend routine screenings recommended by doctors, especially for cervical, breast, oral, and colorectal cancers. Early screening can find disease before severe symptoms appear and improve survival.
Cancer (General).Food: Cancer-friendly food should support strength, immunity, and recovery during treatment. Choose soft, balanced meals with protein such as dal, eggs, curd, fish, or lean meat; include vegetables, fruits, whole grains, nuts, and sufficient fluids. Small frequent meals are often better than large meals when appetite is low. Limit fried foods, processed meats, excess sugar, and alcohol. During chemotherapy or radiation, taste and appetite may change, so adapt meals to tolerance while maintaining calories and protein. A local dietitian or doctor can help adjust food plans safely for each patient.
Cancer (General).Exercise: Regular physical activity helps reduce fatigue, improves mood, supports appetite, and may reduce treatment complications. Most patients can do light activity such as walking 20 to 30 minutes daily, slow stretching, breathing exercises, and simple strength movements with supervision. Activity should match the person's stage, weakness, pain level, and treatment type. Stop exercise if chest pain, severe breathlessness, dizziness, or bleeding occurs. Bedbound patients can still do guided limb movements to prevent stiffness. Safe exercise under medical advice improves quality of life and helps long-term recovery.
Cancer (General).How to control it?: Control requires early diagnosis, correct staging, and treatment at a cancer center or district referral hospital. Treatment may include surgery, chemotherapy, radiotherapy, hormone therapy, targeted therapy, or combinations based on cancer type and stage. Follow treatment schedules strictly and do not stop because of temporary side effects without medical guidance. Manage pain, nutrition, and infections actively. Keep records of reports and medicines. Emotional and family support are important. Palliative care helps symptom relief when cure is not possible. Regular follow-up is essential to detect recurrence early and maintain function.
Cancer (General).When to see a doctor?: Any lump or swelling that does not go away, unexplained weight loss more than 5kg, bleeding from any body part without reason, persistent cough more than 3 weeks, any unusual change in body. Also seek consultation for long fever, severe tiredness, non-healing ulcer, change in voice, or altered bowel habits lasting weeks. People with tobacco use, family history, or previous cancer should not delay. Early hospital visit can prevent late-stage disease, reduce treatment cost, and improve survival. If severe symptoms appear suddenly, visit emergency services immediately.
Cancer (General).Emergency note: Cancer itself may be chronic, but certain warning situations are emergencies and need immediate hospital care. Sudden breathing difficulty, heavy bleeding, confusion, severe uncontrolled pain, inability to swallow fluids, or very high fever during treatment can become life-threatening. Do not wait for home remedies in such cases.
Cancer (General).Emergency signs: Sudden unexplained weight loss; Coughing up blood; Severe pain that does not go away; Difficulty breathing; Sudden swelling in any body part

kannada.What is the disease?: ಕ್ಯಾನ್ಸರ್ ಎಂಬುದು ದೇಹದ ಕೆಲವು ಕೋಶಗಳು ನಿಯಂತ್ರಣವಿಲ್ಲದೆ ಹೆಚ್ಚಾಗಿ ಬೆಳೆಯುವ ರೋಗ. ಇವು ಹತ್ತಿರದ ಭಾಗಗಳಿಗೆ ಅಥವಾ ದೂರದ ಅಂಗಗಳಿಗೆ ಹರಡಬಹುದು. ಇದು ಒಂದೇ ಅಂಗಕ್ಕೆ ಸೀಮಿತವಾಗದೇ ಬಾಯಿ, ಸ್ತನ, ಶ್ವಾಸಕೋಶ, ಹೊಟ್ಟೆ, ರಕ್ತ ಸೇರಿದಂತೆ ಹಲವು ಭಾಗಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಆರಂಭವಾಗಬಹುದು. ಆರಂಭಿಕ ಹಂತದಲ್ಲೇ ಪತ್ತೆಯಾದರೆ ಚಿಕಿತ್ಸೆ ಫಲ ಹೆಚ್ಚು. ಸರಿಯಾದ ಸಮಯದಲ್ಲಿ ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆ, ಹಂತ ನಿರ್ಧಾರ ಮತ್ತು ಚಿಕಿತ್ಸೆ ಪಡೆದರೆ ಅನೇಕರು ದೀರ್ಘಕಾಲ ಉತ್ತಮ ಜೀವನ ನಡೆಸಬಹುದು. ಲಕ್ಷಣಗಳನ್ನು ನಿರ್ಲಕ್ಷಿಸದೇ ವೈದ್ಯರನ್ನು ಸಂಪರ್ಕಿಸುವುದು ಅತ್ಯಂತ ಮುಖ್ಯ.
kannada.What are the symptoms?: ಕ್ಯಾನ್ಸರ್ ಲಕ್ಷಣಗಳು ಯಾವ ಅಂಗದಲ್ಲಿ ಇದೆ ಎಂಬುದರ ಮೇಲೆ ಬದಲಾಗುತ್ತವೆ. ಕಾರಣವಿಲ್ಲದ ತೂಕ ಇಳಿಕೆ, ಕಡಿಮೆಯಾಗದ ದುರ್ಬಲತೆ, ದೀರ್ಘಕಾಲ ಕೆಮ್ಮು, ದೇಹದಲ್ಲಿ ಕಡಿಮೆಯಾಗದ ಗುಡ್ಡೆ, ಕಾರಣವಿಲ್ಲದ ರಕ್ತಸ್ರಾವ, ಬಾಯಿ ಗಾಯ ಗುಣವಾಗದಿರುವುದು, ಮಲಮೂತ್ರ ಚಟುವಟಿಕೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಬದಲಾವಣೆ, ನಿರಂತರ ನೋವು, ಜ್ವರ ಮರುಕಳಿಸುವುದು ಪ್ರಮುಖ ಎಚ್ಚರಿಕೆಗಳು. ಈ ಲಕ್ಷಣಗಳು ಎಲ್ಲವೂ ಕ್ಯಾನ್ಸರ್ ಅಂದೇ ಅರ್ಥವಲ್ಲ; ಆದರೂ ಎರಡು ಮೂರು ವಾರಗಳಿಗಿಂತ ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಮುಂದುವರಿದರೆ ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆ ಮಾಡಿಸಬೇಕು. ಬೇಗ ಪತ್ತೆಯಾದಷ್ಟು ಚಿಕಿತ್ಸೆ ಯಶಸ್ಸು ಹೆಚ್ಚು.
kannada.What causes the disease?: ಧೂಮಪಾನ, ತುಪಾಕಿ ಜಗಿಯುವುದು, ಮದ್ಯಪಾನ, ಅಸಮತೋಲನ ಆಹಾರ, ಅಧಿಕ ತೂಕ, ಕಡಿಮೆ ದೈಹಿಕ ಚಟುವಟಿಕೆ, ಕೆಲವು ವೈರಸ್ ಸೋಂಕುಗಳು (HPV, ಹೆಪಟೈಟಿಸ್), ಕುಟುಂಬದಲ್ಲಿ ಇತಿಹಾಸ, ಕಿರಣೋತ್ಸರ್ಗ ಮತ್ತು ವಿಷಕಾರಿ ರಸಾಯನಗಳಿಗೆ ದೀರ್ಘಕಾಲಿನ ಒಡ್ಡಿಗೆ ಕಾರಣವಾಗಬಹುದು. ಕೆಲವೊಮ್ಮೆ ವಯಸ್ಸಿನ ಕಾರಣದಿಂದಲೂ ಕೋಶಗಳ DNA ದೋಷಗಳು ಹೆಚ್ಚುತ್ತವೆ. ಕಾರಣಗಳು ಮಿಶ್ರವಾಗಿ ಪರಿಣಾಮ ಬೀರುವುದರಿಂದ ಒಂದೇ ಕಾರಣ ಹೇಳಲು ಸಾಧ್ಯವಿಲ್ಲ. ಆದರೆ ಜೀವನಶೈಲಿ ಬದಲಾವಣೆ ಮತ್ತು ನಿಯಮಿತ ತಪಾಸಣೆಗಳಿಂದ ಅಪಾಯವನ್ನು ಕಡಿಮೆ ಮಾಡಬಹುದು.
kannada.Stages: ಹಂತ 1: ಕ್ಯಾನ್ಸರ್ ಸಣ್ಣದು, ಹರಡಿಲ್ಲ. ಹಂತ 2: ಗಾತ್ರ ಹೆಚ್ಚಾಗಿದೆ, ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಹರಡಿಲ್ಲ. ಹಂತ 3: ಹತ್ತಿರದ ಕಣಜಗಳಿಗೆ ಹರಡಿದೆ. ಹಂತ 4: ದೇಹದ ಬೇರೆ ಅಂಗಗಳಿಗೆ ಹರಡಿದೆ, ಇದು ಅತ್ಯಂತ ಗಂಭೀರ ಹಂತ.
kannada.Prevention: ತುಪಾಕಿ ಮತ್ತು ಧೂಮಪಾನ ಸಂಪೂರ್ಣ ನಿಲ್ಲಿಸಿ, ಮದ್ಯಪಾನ ಕಡಿಮೆ ಮಾಡಿ, ತರಕಾರಿ-ಹಣ್ಣು-ಪಲ್ಸ್‌ಗಳುಳ್ಳ ಸಮತೋಲನ ಆಹಾರ ಸೇವಿಸಿ, ದೈನಂದಿನ ವ್ಯಾಯಾಮ ಮಾಡಿ, ತೂಕ ನಿಯಂತ್ರಿಸಿ. ವೈದ್ಯರು ಸಲಹೆ ಮಾಡಿದ ಲಸಿಕೆಗಳು (HPV, ಹೆಪಟೈಟಿಸ್ B) ಪಡೆಯಿರಿ. ಸುರಕ್ಷಿತ ಲೈಂಗಿಕ ಅಭ್ಯಾಸ ಮತ್ತು ಸುರಕ್ಷಿತ ಇಂಜೆಕ್ಷನ್ ಕ್ರಮ ಅನುಸರಿಸಿ. ಕೆಲಸದ ಸ್ಥಳದಲ್ಲಿ ರಾಸಾಯನಿಕ ಒಡ್ಡಿಗೆ ಇದ್ದರೆ ರಕ್ಷಣಾ ಸಾಧನ ಬಳಸಿ. ಅಪಾಯ ಗುಂಪಿನವರು ನಿಯಮಿತ ಸ್ಕ್ರೀನಿಂಗ್ ಮಾಡಿಸಬೇಕು. ಲಕ್ಷಣಗಳು ಮುಂದುವರಿದರೆ ವಿಳಂಬ ಮಾಡಬಾರದು.
kannada.Food: ಚಿಕಿತ್ಸೆಯ ಸಮಯದಲ್ಲಿ ಶಕ್ತಿಯನ್ನು ಉಳಿಸಲು ಪ್ರೋಟೀನ್ ಮತ್ತು ಕ್ಯಾಲೊರಿ ಸಮರ್ಪಕವಾಗಿ ಬೇಕು. ದಾಳು, ಮೊಟ್ಟೆ, ಮೊಸರು, ಮೀನು ಅಥವಾ ತೆಳುವಾದ ಮಾಂಸ, ಜೊತೆಗೆ ತರಕಾರಿ, ಹಣ್ಣು, ಧಾನ್ಯಗಳನ್ನು ಸೇರಿಸಿ. ದಿನಕ್ಕೆ ಹಲವು ಚಿಕ್ಕ ಊಟಗಳು ಉಪಯುಕ್ತ. ಬಾಡಿಸಿದ, ಪ್ಯಾಕೆಟ್, ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಸಕ್ಕರೆ ಮತ್ತು ಮದ್ಯಪಾನ ತಪ್ಪಿಸಿ. ವಾಂತಿ, ಬಾಯಾರಿಕೆ, ರುಚಿ ಬದಲಾವಣೆ ಇದ್ದರೆ ಮೃದುವಾದ ಆಹಾರ ನೀಡಿ. ಸಾಕಷ್ಟು ನೀರು ಕುಡಿಯುವುದು ಮುಖ್ಯ. ವೈಯಕ್ತಿಕ ಪರಿಸ್ಥಿತಿಗೆ ಅನುಗುಣವಾಗಿ ವೈದ್ಯರು ಅಥವಾ ಪೌಷ್ಠಿಕ ತಜ್ಞರ ಸಲಹೆ ಅನುಸರಿಸಿ.
kannada.Exercise: ದಿನವೂ ಲಘು ವ್ಯಾಯಾಮ ಮಾಡಿದರೆ ದಣಿವು ಕಡಿಮೆಯಾಗುತ್ತದೆ, ಮನೋಭಾವ ಉತ್ತಮವಾಗುತ್ತದೆ ಮತ್ತು ದೇಹದ ಕಾರ್ಯಕ್ಷಮತೆ ಹೆಚ್ಚುತ್ತದೆ. ನಿಧಾನವಾಗಿ ನಡೆಯುವುದು, ಉಸಿರಾಟ ವ್ಯಾಯಾಮ, ಸ್ಟ್ರೆಚಿಂಗ್, ತಜ್ಞರ ಮಾರ್ಗದರ್ಶನದ ಸರಳ ಬಲವರ್ಧಕ ವ್ಯಾಯಾಮಗಳು ಸಹಾಯಕ. ಚಿಕಿತ್ಸೆ ಅವಧಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ದೇಹದ ಸ್ಥಿತಿಗೆ ಅನುಗುಣವಾಗಿ ವ್ಯಾಯಾಮ ತೀವ್ರತೆ ಬದಲಿಸಬೇಕು. ಎದೆನೋವು, ತೀವ್ರ ಉಸಿರಾಟದ ತೊಂದರೆ, ತಲೆಸುತ್ತು ಅಥವಾ ರಕ್ತಸ್ರಾವ ಕಂಡರೆ ತಕ್ಷಣ ನಿಲ್ಲಿಸಬೇಕು. ಹಾಸಿಗೆಯಲ್ಲಿರುವವರಿಗೂ ಸಹ ಲಘು ಅಂಗ ಚಲನೆಗಳು ಸಹಕಾರಿ.
kannada.How to control it?: ಮೊದಲು ಸರಿಯಾದ ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆ ಮತ್ತು ಹಂತ ನಿರ್ಧಾರ ಮಾಡಬೇಕು. ನಂತರ ಕ್ಯಾನ್ಸರ್ ಪ್ರಕಾರಕ್ಕೆ ತಕ್ಕಂತೆ ಶಸ್ತ್ರಚಿಕಿತ್ಸೆ, ಕಿಮೋಥೆರಪಿ, ಕಿರಣ ಚಿಕಿತ್ಸೆ, ಹಾರ್ಮೋನ್ ಅಥವಾ ಟಾರ್ಗೆಟ್ ಚಿಕಿತ್ಸೆ ನೀಡಲಾಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಔಷಧಿ ಮತ್ತು ಚಿಕಿತ್ಸೆ ಅವಧಿಯನ್ನು ಮಧ್ಯೆ ನಿಲ್ಲಿಸದೇ ಮುಂದುವರಿಸಬೇಕು. ಪಾರ್ಶ್ವಫಲಗಳು ಇದ್ದರೆ ವೈದ್ಯರಿಗೆ ತಕ್ಷಣ ತಿಳಿಸಿ. ನೋವು ನಿಯಂತ್ರಣ, ಪೌಷ್ಟಿಕ ಆಹಾರ, ಸೋಂಕು ತಡೆ, ಮಾನಸಿಕ ಬೆಂಬಲ ಎಲ್ಲವೂ ಸಮಾನ ಮುಖ್ಯ. ನಿಯಮಿತ ಫಾಲೋ-ಅಪ್ ಮೂಲಕ ಮರುಕಳಿಸುವಿಕೆ ಬೇಗ ಪತ್ತೆಯಾಗಬಹುದು.
kannada.When to see a doctor?: ಕಡಿಮೆಯಾಗದ ಗುಡ್ಡೆ ಅಥವಾ ಊತ, ಕಾರಣವಿಲ್ಲದ 5 ಕೆ.ಜಿ.ಗಿಂತ ಹೆಚ್ಚು ತೂಕ ಇಳಿಕೆ, ಕಾರಣವಿಲ್ಲದ ರಕ್ತಸ್ರಾವ, 3 ವಾರಕ್ಕಿಂತ ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಕೆಮ್ಮು, ದೇಹದಲ್ಲಿ ಅಸಾಮಾನ್ಯ ಬದಲಾವಣೆ ಕಂಡರೆ ವೈದ್ಯರನ್ನು ಸಂಪರ್ಕಿಸಬೇಕು. ಬಾಯಿ ಗಾಯ ಗುಣವಾಗದಿರುವುದು, ನಿರಂತರ ದುರ್ಬಲತೆ, ಧ್ವನಿ ಬದಲಾವಣೆ, ಮಲಮೂತ್ರ ಪದ್ಧತಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ನಿರಂತರ ಬದಲಾವಣೆಗಳೂ ಎಚ್ಚರಿಕೆ. ತುಪಾಕಿ ಬಳಕೆದಾರರು ಮತ್ತು ಕುಟುಂಬ ಇತಿಹಾಸವಿರುವವರು ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆ ವಿಳಂಬ ಮಾಡಬಾರದು. ಬೇಗ ಬಂದರೆ ಚಿಕಿತ್ಸೆಯ ಫಲ ಹೆಚ್ಚು.
kannada.Emergency note: ಕೆಲವು ಕ್ಯಾನ್ಸರ್ ಪರಿಸ್ಥಿತಿಗಳು ತುರ್ತು. ಉಸಿರಾಟ ಕಷ್ಟ, ಹೆಚ್ಚು ರಕ್ತಸ್ರಾವ, ತೀವ್ರ ನೋವು, ಗೊಂದಲ, ದ್ರವ ಕುಡಿಯಲಾರಿಕೆ ಅಥವಾ ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಜ್ವರ ಇದ್ದರೆ ತಕ್ಷಣ ತುರ್ತು ವಿಭಾಗಕ್ಕೆ ಹೋಗಬೇಕು. ಮನೆಮದ್ದುಗಳಿಂದ ಸಮಯ ಕಳೆದುಕೊಳ್ಳಬೇಡಿ.

hindi.What is the disease?: कैंसर ऐसी बीमारी है जिसमें शरीर की कुछ कोशिकाएं नियंत्रण से बाहर बढ़ती हैं और पास के ऊतकों या दूर के अंगों तक फैल सकती हैं। यह मुंह, स्तन, फेफड़े, पेट, खून या शरीर के किसी भी हिस्से में शुरू हो सकता है। हर कैंसर की गति और गंभीरता अलग होती है। शुरुआती जांच में पकड़ आने पर इलाज का परिणाम बेहतर होता है। सही समय पर जांच, स्टेज पता करना और नियमित उपचार से कई मरीज लंबे समय तक सामान्य जीवन जी सकते हैं। लक्षणों को नजरअंदाज करना सबसे बड़ा जोखिम है।
hindi.What are the symptoms?: कैंसर के लक्षण अंग के अनुसार बदलते हैं, लेकिन कुछ सामान्य संकेत हैं: बिना कारण वजन घटना, लंबे समय तक कमजोरी, शरीर में गांठ या सूजन, तीन सप्ताह से अधिक खांसी, बिना कारण खून आना, मुंह का घाव ठीक न होना, मल या पेशाब की आदत में बदलाव, लगातार दर्द, बार-बार बुखार। हर लक्षण कैंसर नहीं होता, पर लगातार बने रहने वाले संकेतों की जांच जरूरी है। ग्रामीण क्षेत्रों में लोग इन लक्षणों को सामान्य कमजोरी समझ लेते हैं, जिससे बीमारी देर से पकड़ी जाती है।
hindi.What causes the disease?: कैंसर के प्रमुख कारणों में तंबाकू सेवन, धूम्रपान, शराब, असंतुलित आहार, मोटापा, कम शारीरिक गतिविधि, कुछ संक्रमण (जैसे HPV, हेपेटाइटिस), पारिवारिक इतिहास, रेडिएशन और रसायनों का संपर्क शामिल हैं। उम्र बढ़ने के साथ कोशिकाओं के DNA में बदलाव भी जोखिम बढ़ाता है। कई बार एक ही कारण नहीं बल्कि कई कारण मिलकर कैंसर बनाते हैं। स्वस्थ जीवनशैली से जोखिम कम किया जा सकता है, लेकिन पूरी तरह खत्म नहीं होता। इसलिए जागरूकता, स्क्रीनिंग और जल्दी जांच बहुत जरूरी है।
hindi.Stages: स्टेज 1: कैंसर छोटा है और फैला नहीं है। स्टेज 2: कैंसर बढ़ा है लेकिन ज्यादा नहीं फैला। स्टेज 3: कैंसर आसपास के ऊतकों तक फैल गया है। स्टेज 4: कैंसर दूसरे अंगों तक फैल गया है, यह सबसे गंभीर अवस्था है।
hindi.Prevention: रोकथाम के लिए तंबाकू और धूम्रपान बंद करें, शराब सीमित रखें, संतुलित भोजन लें, वजन नियंत्रित रखें और रोज व्यायाम करें। डॉक्टर की सलाह के अनुसार HPV और हेपेटाइटिस B जैसे टीके लगवाएं। सुरक्षित यौन व्यवहार और सुरक्षित इंजेक्शन पद्धति अपनाएं। काम पर धूल या रसायनों का संपर्क हो तो सुरक्षा उपकरण उपयोग करें। नियमित स्क्रीनिंग, खासकर मुंह, स्तन, गर्भाशय ग्रीवा और आंत के कैंसर के लिए, शुरुआती पहचान में मदद करती है। किसी भी संदिग्ध लक्षण को नजरअंदाज न करें।
hindi.Food: कैंसर मरीज के लिए पौष्टिक भोजन बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है। प्रोटीन के लिए दाल, अंडा, दही, मछली या कम वसा वाला मांस लें। साथ में हरी सब्जियां, फल, साबुत अनाज और पर्याप्त पानी लें। भूख कम होने पर दिन में छोटे-छोटे भोजन करें। तला-भुना, बहुत मीठा, प्रोसेस्ड भोजन और शराब से बचें। इलाज के दौरान स्वाद बदल सकता है या उल्टी हो सकती है, इसलिए हल्का और सहन होने वाला भोजन दें। सही पोषण से ताकत बनी रहती है और इलाज सहना आसान होता है।
hindi.Exercise: हल्का नियमित व्यायाम कैंसर मरीज में थकान कम करता है, नींद और मनोदशा सुधारता है और मांसपेशियों की ताकत बनाए रखता है। रोज 20-30 मिनट धीरे चलना, सांस के व्यायाम, हल्की स्ट्रेचिंग और डॉक्टर की सलाह से सरल ताकत वाले व्यायाम उपयोगी हैं। मरीज की स्थिति, इलाज और दर्द के अनुसार गतिविधि बदलनी चाहिए। छाती में दर्द, तेज सांस फूलना, चक्कर, या खून आने पर व्यायाम रोक दें। बिस्तर पर रहने वाले मरीज भी फिजियोथेरेपी से लाभ पा सकते हैं।
hindi.How to control it?: कैंसर को नियंत्रित करने के लिए सही जांच, स्टेज निर्धारण और विशेषज्ञ केंद्र में इलाज जरूरी है। उपचार में सर्जरी, कीमोथेरेपी, रेडियोथेरेपी, हार्मोन या टार्गेटेड थेरेपी शामिल हो सकती है। दवाएं और सत्र बीच में न छोड़ें। साइड इफेक्ट होने पर तुरंत डॉक्टर से संपर्क करें। दर्द नियंत्रण, संक्रमण से बचाव, पोषण और मानसिक सहारा बहुत जरूरी हैं। परिवार का सहयोग भी महत्वपूर्ण है। इलाज के बाद नियमित फॉलो-अप से बीमारी की वापसी जल्दी पकड़ी जा सकती है और जीवन गुणवत्ता बेहतर रहती है।
hindi.When to see a doctor?: कोई भी गांठ या सूजन जो ठीक न हो, बिना कारण 5 किलो से ज्यादा वजन घटना, शरीर के किसी भी हिस्से से बिना कारण खून आना, तीन सप्ताह से अधिक खांसी, या शरीर में कोई असामान्य बदलाव दिखे तो तुरंत डॉक्टर से मिलें। मुंह का घाव न भरना, आवाज बदलना, लगातार थकान, मल-पेशाब की आदत में बदलाव भी जांच योग्य संकेत हैं। तंबाकू उपयोग करने वालों और परिवार में कैंसर इतिहास वालों को देर नहीं करनी चाहिए। जल्दी जांच से इलाज की सफलता बढ़ती है।
hindi.Emergency note: कैंसर में कुछ स्थितियां जानलेवा हो सकती हैं। सांस लेने में कठिनाई, ज्यादा खून बहना, बहुत तेज दर्द, भ्रम, तेज बुखार, या पानी भी न पी पाना हो तो तुरंत इमरजेंसी में जाएं। घरेलू उपचार में समय बर्बाद न करें।

Breast Cancer.What is the disease?: Breast cancer is a cancer that starts in breast tissue, usually in milk ducts or glands. It can affect women and, rarely, men. In early stages it may stay only in the breast, but later it can spread to lymph nodes and other organs like bone, lungs, or liver. Many patients are cured when detected early through self-exam and mammography. Delay in seeking care is common due to fear or stigma, especially in rural areas. Any breast change should be checked promptly, even when pain is absent.
Breast Cancer.What are the symptoms?: Common symptoms include a painless lump in breast or armpit, change in breast size or shape, skin dimpling like orange peel, nipple pulling inward, nipple discharge (especially blood-stained), redness, warmth, thickening of skin, or persistent breast pain. Some women feel heaviness in one breast. In advanced disease, weight loss, bone pain, or breathlessness can appear. Not every lump is cancer, but every new lump must be examined by a doctor. Early assessment through clinical exam, imaging, and biopsy is essential for accurate diagnosis.
Breast Cancer.What causes the disease?: Breast cancer risk rises with age, family history, inherited gene mutations (like BRCA), obesity after menopause, alcohol use, lack of physical activity, delayed first childbirth, not breastfeeding, long hormone exposure, and prior chest radiation. Most patients have no single clear cause. Hormonal and genetic factors interact over time and trigger abnormal cell growth. Having risk factors does not guarantee disease, and absence of risk factors does not mean zero risk. Therefore awareness, monthly self-check, and regular screening are important for early diagnosis and better treatment outcomes.
Breast Cancer.Stages: Stage 0: Abnormal cells present but not spread (DCIS). Stage 1: Tumor is small (up to 2cm) only in breast. Stage 2: Tumor is 2-5cm or spread to nearby lymph nodes. Stage 3: Tumor has spread to chest wall or many lymph nodes. Stage 4: Cancer has spread to other organs like lungs, bones, liver.
Breast Cancer.Prevention: Risk can be reduced by regular self breast examination every month, mammogram screening after age 40, maintain healthy weight, limit alcohol consumption, breastfeeding reduces risk, exercise regularly. Also avoid tobacco, take balanced food, and seek medical advice if family history exists. Women with high risk may need earlier screening plans. Community awareness and reducing stigma help timely diagnosis. Prevention does not mean complete guarantee, so any suspicious change must still be evaluated quickly even if screening was previously normal.
Breast Cancer.Food: A breast-cancer supportive diet should include vegetables, fruits, whole grains, pulses, nuts, and adequate protein from dal, eggs, fish, soy, milk, or lean meat. Reduce processed foods, deep-fried items, red meat excess, sugary drinks, and alcohol. During treatment, appetite may reduce; small frequent meals and enough fluids help maintain strength. Include iron and calcium sources where needed. If mouth sores or nausea occur, use soft, bland foods. Nutrition should be individualized, especially in diabetes or kidney disease. Good nutrition improves treatment tolerance and recovery.
Breast Cancer.Exercise: Regular activity lowers recurrence risk and improves energy, mood, and mobility. Recommended options include brisk walking 30 minutes most days, light strength exercises 2 to 3 times weekly, stretching for shoulder stiffness after surgery, and breathing exercises. Post-surgery arm exercises should begin under physiotherapist guidance to avoid lymphedema and improve range of motion. Avoid very heavy lifting in the affected arm until cleared by doctor. If severe pain, swelling, dizziness, or breathlessness occurs, stop and seek medical advice. Exercise should be gradual and consistent.
Breast Cancer.How to control it?: Control requires multidisciplinary care: surgery, chemotherapy, radiotherapy, hormone therapy, targeted therapy, or immunotherapy depending on subtype and stage. Complete planned treatment cycles and follow-up visits. Manage side effects such as nausea, hair loss, fatigue, and low immunity with medical support, not self-medication. Protect the operated arm from injury or tight pressure to reduce swelling risk. Emotional support, counseling, and support groups help adherence. Keep pathology and scan reports safely. Early treatment and long-term follow-up significantly improve survival and quality of life.
Breast Cancer.When to see a doctor?: Any lump in breast even if not painful, Change in breast shape or size, Nipple discharge without pregnancy, Skin dimpling on breast, Redness or thickening of breast skin. Also seek care for nipple inversion, persistent breast pain, or swelling near armpit. Women with family history or previous breast disease should not delay even mild symptoms. Early clinical exam and imaging can identify treatable disease. Waiting for pain before consulting is unsafe because many early breast cancers are painless.
Breast Cancer.Emergency note: Breast cancer usually needs urgent specialist care rather than panic, but some signs require emergency attention: sudden severe swelling, high fever with breast infection, breathing difficulty, heavy bleeding, or severe uncontrolled pain. If these occur, go to emergency immediately.
Breast Cancer.Emergency signs: Sudden large lump in breast; Nipple discharge with blood; Severe breast pain; Skin of breast turning red and swollen suddenly; Arm swelling near armpit

kannada.What is the disease?: ಸ್ತನ ಕ್ಯಾನ್ಸರ್ ಸ್ತನದ ನಾಳಿಗಳು ಅಥವಾ ಗ್ರಂಥಿಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಶುರುವಾಗುವ ಗಂಭೀರ ರೋಗ. ಆರಂಭದಲ್ಲಿ ಇದು ಸ್ತನದಲ್ಲೇ ಇರಬಹುದು, ನಂತರ ಕಕ್ಷಾ ಲಿಂಫ್ ನೋಡ್‌ಗಳಿಗೆ ಹಾಗೂ ಎಲುಬು, ಶ್ವಾಸಕೋಶ, ಯಕೃತ್‌ಗಳಿಗೆ ಹರಡಬಹುದು. ಬೇಗ ಪತ್ತೆಯಾದರೆ ಸಂಪೂರ್ಣ ಚಿಕಿತ್ಸೆ ಸಾಧ್ಯತೆ ಹೆಚ್ಚು. ಹಲವರು ನೋವು ಇಲ್ಲದಿದ್ದರಿಂದ ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆ ಮುಂದೂಡುತ್ತಾರೆ, ಇದು ಅಪಾಯಕರ. ಮಹಿಳೆಯರಿಗೆ ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಕಂಡರೂ ಪುರುಷರಿಗೂ ಅಪರೂಪವಾಗಿ ಆಗಬಹುದು. ತಿಂಗಳಿಗೆ ಸ್ವಯಂ ಸ್ತನ ಪರಿಶೀಲನೆ ಮತ್ತು ವಯಸ್ಸಿನ ನಂತರ ಮ್ಯಾಮೋಗ್ರಾಂ ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆ ಜೀವ ರಕ್ಷಕ.
kannada.What are the symptoms?: ಸ್ತನದಲ್ಲಿ ನೋವಿಲ್ಲದ ಗುಡ್ಡೆ, ಕಕ್ಷೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಊತ, ಸ್ತನದ ಗಾತ್ರ/ಆಕೃತಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಬದಲಾವಣೆ, ಚರ್ಮ ಕುಳಿತಂತೆ ಕಾಣುವುದು, ನಿಪ್ಪಲ್ ಒಳಗೆ ಸೆಳೆತ, ರಕ್ತ ಮಿಶ್ರಿತ ನಿಪ್ಪಲ್ ಸ್ರಾವ, ಸ್ತನ ಚರ್ಮ ದಪ್ಪವಾಗುವುದು ಅಥವಾ ಕೆಂಪಾಗುವುದು ಪ್ರಮುಖ ಲಕ್ಷಣಗಳು. ಕೆಲವರಿಗೆ ನಿರಂತರ ನೋವು ಅಥವಾ ಭಾರವಾಗಿರುವ ಭಾವನೆ ಕಾಣಬಹುದು. ಎಲ್ಲ ಗುಡ್ಡೆಗಳೂ ಕ್ಯಾನ್ಸರ್ ಅಲ್ಲ; ಆದರೂ ಪ್ರತಿಯೊಂದು ಹೊಸ ಬದಲಾವಣೆಯೂ ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆಗೆ ಒಳಪಡಬೇಕು. ವಿಳಂಬವಾಗಿದರೆ ಮುಂದಿನ ಹಂತಕ್ಕೆ ಹೋಗುವ ಸಾಧ್ಯತೆ ಹೆಚ್ಚು.
kannada.What causes the disease?: ವಯಸ್ಸು, ಕುಟುಂಬ ಇತಿಹಾಸ, BRCA ಜೀನ್ ದೋಷ, ಅಧಿಕ ತೂಕ, ಮದ್ಯಪಾನ, ಕಡಿಮೆ ವ್ಯಾಯಾಮ, ಸಂತಾನೋತ್ಪತ್ತಿ ಮಾದರಿಯ ಹಾರ್ಮೋನ್ ಪರಿಣಾಮಗಳು, ತಾಯ್ತನದ ನಂತರ ಹಾಲುಣಿಸದಿರುವುದು, ಹಿಂದಿನ ಕಿರಣ ಚಿಕಿತ್ಸೆ ಮುಂತಾದವು ಅಪಾಯ ಹೆಚ್ಚಿಸಬಹುದು. ಒಂದೇ ಕಾರಣದಿಂದ ಮಾತ್ರ ಈ ರೋಗ ಆಗುವುದಿಲ್ಲ; ಅನೇಕ ಕಾರಣಗಳು ಸೇರಿ ಪರಿಣಾಮ ಬೀರುತ್ತವೆ. ಕೆಲವರಿಗೆ ಯಾವುದೇ ಸ್ಪಷ್ಟ ಅಪಾಯಕಾರಕ ಇಲ್ಲದಿದ್ದರೂ ರೋಗ ಬರಬಹುದು. ಆದ್ದರಿಂದ ನಿಯಮಿತ ಸ್ವಪರಿಶೀಲನೆ ಮತ್ತು ವೈದ್ಯಕೀಯ ತಪಾಸಣೆ ಬಹಳ ಮುಖ್ಯ.
kannada.Stages: ಹಂತ 0: ಅಸಾಮಾನ್ಯ ಕೋಶಗಳು ಮಾತ್ರ, ಹರಡುವಿಕೆ ಇಲ್ಲ (DCIS). ಹಂತ 1: 2 ಸೆಂ.ಮೀ.ವರೆಗೆ ಸಣ್ಣ ಗುಡ್ಡೆ, ಸ್ತನದಲ್ಲೇ. ಹಂತ 2: 2-5 ಸೆಂ.ಮೀ. ಗುಡ್ಡೆ ಅಥವಾ ಹತ್ತಿರದ ಲಿಂಫ್ ನೋಡ್‌ಗೆ ಹರಡು. ಹಂತ 3: ಎದೆಗೋಡೆ ಅಥವಾ ಅನೇಕ ಲಿಂಫ್ ನೋಡ್‌ಗಳಿಗೆ ಹರಡು. ಹಂತ 4: ಶ್ವಾಸಕೋಶ, ಎಲುಬು, ಯಕೃತ್ ಮುಂತಾದ ಅಂಗಗಳಿಗೆ ಹರಡು.
kannada.Prevention: ಪ್ರತಿ ತಿಂಗಳು ಸ್ವಯಂ ಸ್ತನ ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆ ಮಾಡಿ, 40 ವರ್ಷ ನಂತರ ಮ್ಯಾಮೋಗ್ರಾಂ ಸ್ಕ್ರೀನಿಂಗ್ ಮಾಡಿಸಿ, ತೂಕ ನಿಯಂತ್ರಿಸಿ, ಮದ್ಯಪಾನ ಕಡಿಮೆ ಮಾಡಿ, ಮಕ್ಕಳಿಗೆ ತಾಯಿ ಹಾಲುಣಿಸುವುದು ಅಪಾಯ ಕಡಿಮೆ ಮಾಡುತ್ತದೆ, ನಿಯಮಿತ ವ್ಯಾಯಾಮ ಮಾಡಿ. ತುಪಾಕಿ ತಪ್ಪಿಸಿ ಮತ್ತು ಸಮತೋಲನ ಆಹಾರ ಸೇವಿಸಿ. ಕುಟುಂಬ ಇತಿಹಾಸ ಇದ್ದವರಿಗೆ ಬೇಗ ಮತ್ತು ನಿಯಮಿತ ಸ್ಕ್ರೀನಿಂಗ್ ಅಗತ್ಯ. ತಡೆ ಕ್ರಮಗಳಿದ್ದರೂ ಲಕ್ಷಣ ಕಂಡರೆ ತಕ್ಷಣ ವೈದ್ಯರನ್ನು ಸಂಪರ್ಕಿಸಬೇಕು.
kannada.Food: ಪೌಷ್ಟಿಕ ಆಹಾರ ಚಿಕಿತ್ಸೆ ವೇಳೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ದೇಹದ ಶಕ್ತಿ ಉಳಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ತರಕಾರಿ, ಹಣ್ಣು, ಸಂಪೂರ್ಣ ಧಾನ್ಯಗಳು, ಪಲ್ಸ್, ಕಾಯಿ ಬೀಜಗಳು, ಜೊತೆಗೆ ದಾಳು/ಮೊಟ್ಟೆ/ಮೀನು/ಹಾಲುಗಳಿಂದ ಪ್ರೋಟೀನ್ ಪಡೆಯಿರಿ. ಬಾಡಿಸಿದ ಮತ್ತು ಪ್ಯಾಕೆಟ್ ಆಹಾರ, ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಸಕ್ಕರೆ, ಮದ್ಯಪಾನ ಕಡಿಮೆ ಮಾಡಿ. ಭುಖೆ ಕಡಿಮೆ ಇದ್ದರೆ ಚಿಕ್ಕ ಚಿಕ್ಕ ಊಟಗಳನ್ನು ಹೆಚ್ಚಿಸಿ. ವಾಂತಿ ಅಥವಾ ಬಾಯಿ ನೋವು ಇದ್ದರೆ ಮೃದುವಾದ ಆಹಾರ ಸೇವಿಸಿ. ಮಧುಮೇಹ ಅಥವಾ ಬೇರೆ ರೋಗ ಇದ್ದರೆ ವೈದ್ಯರ ಸಲಹೆಗೆ ಅನುಗುಣ ಆಹಾರ ಯೋಜನೆ ಪಾಲಿಸಿ.
kannada.Exercise: ದಿನನಿತ್ಯ ನಡೆಯುವುದು, ಹಗುರವಾದ ಬಲವರ್ಧಕ ವ್ಯಾಯಾಮ, ಸ್ಟ್ರೆಚಿಂಗ್ ಮತ್ತು ಶ್ವಾಸ ವ್ಯಾಯಾಮಗಳು ಉಪಯುಕ್ತ. ಶಸ್ತ್ರಚಿಕಿತ್ಸೆಯ ನಂತರ ಭುಜದ ಚಲನೆ ಕಡಿಮೆಯಾಗಬಹುದು; ಫಿಸಿಯೋ ಮಾರ್ಗದರ್ಶನದಲ್ಲಿ ಕೈ ವ್ಯಾಯಾಮ ಆರಂಭಿಸಬೇಕು. ಕಕ್ಷಾ ಊತ ತಪ್ಪಿಸಲು ಭಾರವಾದ ವಸ್ತುಗಳನ್ನು ತಕ್ಷಣ ಎತ್ತಬೇಡಿ. ತಲೆ ಸುತ್ತುವುದು, ತೀವ್ರ ನೋವು, ಉಸಿರಾಟ ತೊಂದರೆ ಇದ್ದರೆ ವ್ಯಾಯಾಮ ನಿಲ್ಲಿಸಿ. ನಿಯಮಿತ ವ್ಯಾಯಾಮ ಮರುಕಳಿಸುವ ಅಪಾಯ ಕಡಿಮೆ ಮಾಡಲು ಸಹಾಯಕ ಎಂದು ಅಧ್ಯಯನಗಳು ಸೂಚಿಸುತ್ತವೆ.
kannada.How to control it?: ರೋಗ ನಿಯಂತ್ರಣಕ್ಕೆ ಶಸ್ತ್ರಚಿಕಿತ್ಸೆ, ಕಿಮೋಥೆರಪಿ, ಕಿರಣ ಚಿಕಿತ್ಸೆ, ಹಾರ್ಮೋನ್/ಟಾರ್ಗೆಟ್ ಚಿಕಿತ್ಸೆಗಳನ್ನು ಹಂತ ಮತ್ತು ಪ್ರಕಾರಕ್ಕೆ ತಕ್ಕಂತೆ ನೀಡಲಾಗುತ್ತದೆ. ವೈದ್ಯರು ಸೂಚಿಸಿದ ಸೈಕಲ್‌ಗಳನ್ನು ಪೂರ್ಣಗೊಳಿಸಬೇಕು. ಪಾರ್ಶ್ವಫಲಗಳು ಇದ್ದರೆ ಚಿಕಿತ್ಸೆ ನಿಲ್ಲಿಸದೇ ವೈದ್ಯರನ್ನು ಸಂಪರ್ಕಿಸಿ ನಿರ್ವಹಣೆ ಮಾಡಿಸಬೇಕು. ಆಪರೇಷನ್ ಮಾಡಿದ ಕೈಗೆ ಗಾಯ/ಒತ್ತಡ ತಪ್ಪಿಸಿ. ನಿಯಮಿತ ಫಾಲೋ-ಅಪ್ ಮೂಲಕ ಮರುಕಳಿಸುವಿಕೆ ಬೇಗ ಪತ್ತೆಯಾಗಬಹುದು. ಕುಟುಂಬ ಮತ್ತು ಮಾನಸಿಕ ಬೆಂಬಲವೂ ಪ್ರಮುಖ.
kannada.When to see a doctor?: ನೋವಿಲ್ಲದಿದ್ದರೂ ಸ್ತನದಲ್ಲಿ ಯಾವುದೇ ಗುಡ್ಡೆ ಕಂಡರೆ, ಸ್ತನದ ಗಾತ್ರ ಅಥವಾ ಆಕಾರ ಬದಲಾಗಿದ್ರೆ, ಗರ್ಭಧಾರಣೆ ಇಲ್ಲದೆ ನಿಪ್ಪಲ್ ಸ್ರಾವ ಕಂಡರೆ, ಸ್ತನ ಚರ್ಮ ಕುಳಿತಂತೆ ಕಂಡರೆ, ಕೆಂಪು ಅಥವಾ ದಪ್ಪ ಚರ್ಮ ಕಂಡರೆ ತಕ್ಷಣ ವೈದ್ಯರನ್ನು ಸಂಪರ್ಕಿಸಬೇಕು. ಕಕ್ಷಾ ಊತ, ನಿಪ್ಪಲ್ ಒಳಗೆ ಹೋಗುವುದು, ನಿರಂತರ ನೋವು ಕೂಡ ಪರಿಶೀಲನೆಗೆ ಕಾರಣ. ಬೇಗ ತಪಾಸಣೆ ಮಾಡಿದರೆ ಚಿಕಿತ್ಸೆಯ ಯಶಸ್ಸು ಹೆಚ್ಚುತ್ತದೆ.
kannada.Emergency note: ಸ್ತನ ಕ್ಯಾನ್ಸರ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ ಕೆಲವು ಲಕ್ಷಣಗಳು ತುರ್ತು: ಅಕಸ್ಮಾತ್ ದೊಡ್ಡ ಊತ, ರಕ್ತಸ್ರಾವ, ತೀವ್ರ ನೋವು, ಜ್ವರದೊಂದಿಗೆ ಕೆಂಪು-ಸೂಜು, ಉಸಿರಾಟದ ತೊಂದರೆ. ಇವು ಕಂಡರೆ ತುರ್ತು ಚಿಕಿತ್ಸೆಗೆ ಹೋಗಬೇಕು.

hindi.What is the disease?: स्तन कैंसर स्तन की नलिकाओं या ग्रंथियों से शुरू होने वाला कैंसर है। शुरुआत में यह केवल स्तन तक सीमित हो सकता है, लेकिन समय पर इलाज न मिलने पर बगल की लिम्फ नोड और बाद में फेफड़े, हड्डी या लिवर तक फैल सकता है। यह महिलाओं में अधिक होता है, पर पुरुषों में भी दुर्लभ रूप से हो सकता है। शुरुआती पहचान से इलाज का परिणाम बहुत बेहतर होता है। दर्द न होने पर भी गांठ गंभीर हो सकती है, इसलिए किसी भी बदलाव को नजरअंदाज नहीं करना चाहिए।
hindi.What are the symptoms?: स्तन या बगल में नई गांठ, स्तन का आकार बदलना, त्वचा में गड्ढा पड़ना, निप्पल अंदर धंसना, निप्पल से खून जैसा स्राव, त्वचा का लाल या मोटा होना, एक तरफ लगातार दर्द या भारीपन जैसे लक्षण दिख सकते हैं। हर गांठ कैंसर नहीं होती, पर हर नई गांठ की जांच जरूरी है। उन्नत अवस्था में वजन घटना, हड्डियों में दर्द, सांस फूलना भी हो सकता है। जल्दी जांच से बीमारी शुरुआती स्टेज में पकड़कर बेहतर उपचार संभव होता है।
hindi.What causes the disease?: उम्र बढ़ना, परिवार में स्तन कैंसर इतिहास, BRCA जीन परिवर्तन, मोटापा, शराब, शारीरिक निष्क्रियता, लंबे समय तक हार्मोनल प्रभाव, देर से गर्भधारण, स्तनपान न करना, और पूर्व रेडिएशन जोखिम बढ़ाते हैं। अधिकतर मामलों में एक ही कारण नहीं मिलता। हार्मोन, आनुवंशिकता और जीवनशैली मिलकर प्रभाव डालते हैं। जोखिम कारक होने का मतलब निश्चित कैंसर नहीं, और जोखिम न होने पर भी कैंसर संभव है। इसलिए नियमित जांच, स्व-परीक्षण और जागरूकता आवश्यक है।
hindi.Stages: स्टेज 0: असामान्य कोशिकाएं हैं, फैली नहीं (DCIS)। स्टेज 1: 2 सेमी तक छोटी गांठ, केवल स्तन में। स्टेज 2: 2-5 सेमी गांठ या पास की लिम्फ नोड तक फैलाव। स्टेज 3: छाती की दीवार या कई लिम्फ नोड तक फैलाव। स्टेज 4: फेफड़े, हड्डी, लिवर जैसे अंगों तक फैलाव।
hindi.Prevention: नियमित self breast examination every month करें, mammogram screening after age 40 कराएं, maintain healthy weight रखें, limit alcohol consumption करें, breastfeeding reduces risk, exercise regularly करें। साथ में तंबाकू से दूर रहें और संतुलित भोजन लें। यदि परिवार में इतिहास है तो डॉक्टर से व्यक्तिगत स्क्रीनिंग योजना बनवाएं। रोकथाम पूर्ण सुरक्षा नहीं देती, इसलिए किसी भी संदिग्ध बदलाव पर तुरंत जांच कराएं।
hindi.Food: उपचार के दौरान शरीर को ताकत देने के लिए प्रोटीन और संतुलित पोषण जरूरी है। दाल, अंडा, दही, मछली, सोया, सब्जियां, फल, साबुत अनाज और पर्याप्त पानी लें। तला-भुना, बहुत मीठा, प्रोसेस्ड भोजन और शराब से बचें। भूख कम हो तो छोटे-छोटे भोजन करें। उल्टी या मुंह में छाले होने पर नरम भोजन लें। मधुमेह या अन्य बीमारी के साथ भोजन योजना डॉक्टर या डाइटिशियन के अनुसार रखें। अच्छा पोषण उपचार सहनशीलता और रिकवरी में मदद करता है।
hindi.Exercise: रोज चलना, हल्का स्ट्रेचिंग, सांस के व्यायाम और डॉक्टर की सलाह से हल्के strength exercises उपयोगी हैं। सर्जरी के बाद कंधे की जकड़न कम करने के लिए फिजियोथेरेपी महत्वपूर्ण है। बगल में सूजन जोखिम होने पर प्रभावित हाथ से भारी वजन न उठाएं। थकान, चक्कर, तेज दर्द या सांस फूलने पर व्यायाम रोकें। नियमित और सुरक्षित गतिविधि से ऊर्जा, नींद और मानसिक स्थिति में सुधार आता है तथा दीर्घकालीन परिणाम बेहतर होते हैं।
hindi.How to control it?: नियंत्रण के लिए सही स्टेजिंग और विशेषज्ञ टीम द्वारा उपचार जरूरी है। इलाज में सर्जरी, कीमोथेरेपी, रेडियोथेरेपी, हार्मोन थेरेपी या टार्गेटेड थेरेपी शामिल हो सकती है। दवाएं बीच में बंद न करें। साइड इफेक्ट होने पर डॉक्टर से प्रबंधन लें। ऑपरेशन वाले हाथ की देखभाल करें और संक्रमण से बचें। नियमित फॉलो-अप और स्कैन से बीमारी की वापसी जल्दी पकड़ी जा सकती है। परिवार का सहयोग और मानसिक समर्थन उपचार पूरा करने में बहुत मदद करता है।
hindi.When to see a doctor?: स्तन में कोई भी गांठ, चाहे दर्द न हो; स्तन का आकार/आकृति बदलना; गर्भावस्था बिना निप्पल स्राव; त्वचा में गड्ढा; स्तन की त्वचा का लाल या मोटा होना—इन सभी स्थितियों में डॉक्टर से तुरंत मिलें। निप्पल अंदर जाना, बगल में सूजन या लगातार दर्द भी जांच योग्य हैं। जल्दी जांच से उपचार सरल, सस्ता और सफल होने की संभावना अधिक रहती है।
hindi.Emergency note: अचानक बहुत बड़ी गांठ, खून वाला स्राव, तेज दर्द, तेज बुखार के साथ लाल सूजन, या सांस लेने में तकलीफ हो तो इसे इमरजेंसी मानें और तुरंत अस्पताल जाएं।

Parkinsons Disease.What is the disease?: Parkinsons disease is a long-term neurological disorder where brain cells that produce dopamine gradually reduce. Dopamine helps smooth body movement, balance, and coordination. When dopamine falls, a person develops shaking (tremor), stiffness, slowness, and walking difficulty. The disease usually starts slowly and progresses over years. It is more common after age 60, but younger adults can also be affected. Parkinsons is not contagious. Although cure is not currently available, medicines, physiotherapy, speech therapy, nutrition, and family support can control symptoms and improve quality of life for many years.
Parkinsons Disease.What are the symptoms?: Early symptoms may include one-hand resting tremor, reduced arm swing while walking, slowness in daily work, stiffness in limbs, soft or low speech, mask-like face, small handwriting (micrographia), sleep disturbance, constipation, low mood, and loss of smell. As disease progresses, balance problems, freezing episodes, falls, swallowing difficulty, and memory or behavior changes can occur. Symptoms often begin on one side and later involve both sides. Not all patients have tremor. Because signs develop slowly, families may think it is normal aging, which delays diagnosis and treatment.
Parkinsons Disease.What causes the disease?: Exact cause is not fully known. It is linked to degeneration of dopamine-producing neurons in the substantia nigra part of the brain. Risk may increase with older age, family history, certain genetic mutations, repeated pesticide exposure, and environmental toxins. Head injury and chronic inflammation may also play a role in some people. Most cases are sporadic and not directly inherited. Parkinsons is not caused by weakness or stress alone, though stress can worsen symptoms. Early neurologist assessment helps confirm diagnosis and rule out other conditions that mimic Parkinsons symptoms.
Parkinsons Disease.Stages: Stage 1: Mild symptoms on one side of body only. Stage 2: Symptoms on both sides, balance still normal. Stage 3: Balance affected, falls possible, independent living. Stage 4: Severe symptoms, needs help for daily activities. Stage 5: Cannot stand or walk, needs full time care.
Parkinsons Disease.Prevention: No proven prevention but these reduce risk: Regular aerobic exercise, Green tea and antioxidant rich foods, Avoid exposure to pesticides and chemicals, Head injury prevention (wear helmets), Stay mentally and socially active. Also control blood pressure, diabetes, and sleep problems for healthy brain aging. These measures may not completely stop disease, but they support brain function and can delay disability. People with family history should seek early evaluation if subtle tremor, slowness, or smell loss appears.
Parkinsons Disease.Food: Diet should support mobility, bowel function, and medicine response. Use fiber-rich foods like vegetables, fruits, whole grains, and pulses to reduce constipation. Ensure adequate protein, but in some patients levodopa works better when protein is spread across meals; follow doctor guidance. Drink enough water to prevent dehydration and low blood pressure. Include nuts, seeds, and healthy oils for energy. If swallowing is difficult, use soft or semi-solid foods and speech therapist advice. Limit excessive processed food, very salty snacks, and uncontrolled sugar intake.
Parkinsons Disease.Exercise: Walking daily for 30 minutes, Tai Chi for balance improvement, Swimming for muscle strength, Dancing to improve coordination, Stretching exercises for stiffness, Speech therapy exercises. In addition, posture training, sit-to-stand practice, and cue-based gait practice can reduce freezing and falls. Exercise should be supervised initially by physiotherapist and adapted to disease stage. Consistency is more important than intensity. Even in advanced stages, gentle assisted movement prevents stiffness, bed sores, and mood decline.
Parkinsons Disease.How to control it?: Control relies on long-term neurologist follow-up, regular medicines (such as levodopa combinations), physiotherapy, speech and swallowing therapy, and home safety modifications. Take medicines on time daily; missed doses can worsen mobility suddenly. Manage non-motor issues like constipation, depression, sleep problems, and hallucinations with medical guidance. Remove fall hazards at home, use support rails, and monitor blood pressure during posture changes. Caregiver education is essential because symptoms fluctuate. In selected advanced patients, deep brain stimulation may be considered at specialized centers.
Parkinsons Disease.When to see a doctor?: Trembling or shaking in hands at rest, Stiffness in arms or legs, Slow movement in daily activities, Balance problems and frequent falls, Small handwriting (micrographia), Soft or slurred speech, Loss of smell. Also consult if swallowing becomes difficult, frequent choking occurs, confusion appears, or medicines seem ineffective. Early neurologist diagnosis improves symptom control and helps maintain independence for longer. Do not assume all shaking in elderly is normal aging; timely evaluation can prevent avoidable complications.
Parkinsons Disease.Emergency note: Parkinsons is usually chronic, but sudden severe events need emergency care. If the patient cannot swallow medicines or food, develops high fever with rigidity, sudden confusion, repeated falls, injury, or severe breathing difficulty, immediate hospital management is required. Delayed care can cause life-threatening complications.
Parkinsons Disease.Emergency signs: Sudden inability to swallow or breathe; Severe confusion or hallucinations; Complete inability to move (freezing episode); High fever with muscle stiffness (neuroleptic crisis); Sudden fall with head injury

kannada.What is the disease?: ಪಾರ್ಕಿನ್ಸನ್ ರೋಗವು ಮೆದುಳಿನ ಡೋಪಮೈನ್ ಉತ್ಪಾದಕ ಕೋಶಗಳು ನಿಧಾನವಾಗಿ ಕಡಿಮೆಯಾಗುವುದರಿಂದ ಉಂಟಾಗುವ ದೀರ್ಘಕಾಲೀನ ನರರೋಗ. ಇದರ ಪರಿಣಾಮವಾಗಿ ಕೈ ನಡುಕು, ದೇಹ ಕಟ್ಟುತನ, ಚಲನೆಯ ನಿಧಾನತೆ, ಸಮತೋಲನ ಸಮಸ್ಯೆ ಉಂಟಾಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಆರಂಭದಲ್ಲಿ ಲಕ್ಷಣಗಳು ಸಣ್ಣದಾಗಿದ್ದು ವರ್ಷಗಳ ಕಾಲ ನಿಧಾನವಾಗಿ ಹೆಚ್ಚಾಗುತ್ತವೆ. ಇದು ಸಾಂಕ್ರಾಮಿಕವಲ್ಲ. ಸಂಪೂರ್ಣ ಗುಣಪಡಿಸುವ ಚಿಕಿತ್ಸೆ ಇಲ್ಲದಿದ್ದರೂ ಔಷಧಿ, ಫಿಸಿಯೋಥೆರಪಿ, ಮಾತಿನ ಚಿಕಿತ್ಸೆ ಮತ್ತು ಮನೆಯ ಬೆಂಬಲದಿಂದ ರೋಗಿಯನ್ನು ದೀರ್ಘಕಾಲ ಸ್ವಾವಲಂಬಿಯಾಗಿ ಇರಿಸಬಹುದು.
kannada.What are the symptoms?: ವಿಶ್ರಾಂತಿ ಸ್ಥಿತಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಕೈ ನಡುಕು, ನಡೆಯುವಾಗ ಕೈ ಊಗುವುದು ಕಡಿಮೆಯಾಗುವುದು, ನಿಧಾನ ಚಲನೆ, ಕೈ-ಕಾಲುಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಕಟ್ಟುತನ, ಮೃದು ಧ್ವನಿ, ಸಣ್ಣ ಅಕ್ಷರದಲ್ಲಿ ಬರೆಯುವುದು, ಮುಖದಲ್ಲಿ ಅಭಿವ್ಯಕ್ತಿ ಕಡಿಮೆ, ನಿದ್ರೆ ಸಮಸ್ಯೆ, ಮಲಬದ್ದತೆ, ವಾಸನೆ ಅರಿವಿನ ಕಡಿಮೆತನ ಪ್ರಮುಖ ಲಕ್ಷಣಗಳು. ನಂತರ ಹಂತಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಸಮತೋಲನ ತಪ್ಪುವುದು, ಬಿದ್ದುಕೊಳ್ಳುವುದು, ಚಲನೆ ಅಚಾನಕ್ ನಿಲ್ಲುವುದು (freezing), ನುಂಗುವ ತೊಂದರೆ, ಗೊಂದಲ/ಭ್ರಮೆಗಳೂ ಕಾಣಬಹುದು. ಎಲ್ಲಾ ರೋಗಿಗಳಲ್ಲೂ ನಡುಕು ಇರಲೇಬೇಕು ಎಂದಿಲ್ಲ.
kannada.What causes the disease?: ಖಚಿತ ಕಾರಣ ಸಂಪೂರ್ಣ ತಿಳಿದಿಲ್ಲ. ಮೆದುಳಿನ substantia nigra ಭಾಗದ ಡೋಪಮೈನ್ ಕೋಶಗಳು ಹಾನಿಗೊಳಗಾದಾಗ ರೋಗ ಪ್ರಾರಂಭವಾಗುತ್ತದೆ. ವಯಸ್ಸು, ಕುಟುಂಬ ಇತಿಹಾಸ, ಕೆಲವು ಜನ್ಯ ಬದಲಾವಣೆಗಳು, ಪೆಸ್ಟಿಸೈಡ್/ರಸಾಯನಿಕ ಒಡ್ಡಿಗೆ, ತಲೆಯ ಗಾಯ ಇತ್ಯಾದಿ ಅಪಾಯ ಹೆಚ್ಚಿಸಬಹುದು. ಬಹಳ ಸಂದರ್ಭಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಒಂದೇ ಕಾರಣದಿಂದ ಅಲ್ಲ, ಹಲವು ಕಾರಣಗಳ ಮಿಶ್ರ ಪರಿಣಾಮವಾಗಿರುತ್ತದೆ. ಇದು ದುರ್ಬಲ ಮನೋಬಲದಿಂದಾಗುವುದಿಲ್ಲ; ಆದರೆ ಒತ್ತಡ ಲಕ್ಷಣಗಳನ್ನು ಹೆಚ್ಚಿಸಬಹುದು. ಬೇಗ ನರರೋಗ ತಜ್ಞರ ಮೌಲ್ಯಮಾಪನ ಮುಖ್ಯ.
kannada.Stages: ಹಂತ 1: ಒಂದು ಬದಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಮಾತ್ರ ಸಣ್ಣ ಲಕ್ಷಣಗಳು. ಹಂತ 2: ಎರಡೂ ಬದಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಲಕ್ಷಣಗಳು, ಸಮತೋಲನ ಸಾಮಾನ್ಯ. ಹಂತ 3: ಸಮತೋಲನ ಹಾನಿ, ಬಿದ್ದುವ ಅಪಾಯ, ಆದರೆ ಸ್ವತಂತ್ರ ಜೀವನ ಸಾಧ್ಯ. ಹಂತ 4: ತೀವ್ರ ಲಕ್ಷಣಗಳು, ದಿನನಿತ್ಯ ಕೆಲಸಕ್ಕೆ ಸಹಾಯ ಅಗತ್ಯ. ಹಂತ 5: ನಿಲ್ಲಲು/ನಡೆಯಲು ಸಾಧ್ಯವಿಲ್ಲ, ಪೂರ್ಣ ಕಾಲದ ಆರೈಕೆ ಬೇಕು.
kannada.Prevention: ನಿರ್ದಿಷ್ಟ ತಡೆ ವಿಧಾನ ಇಲ್ಲ, ಆದರೆ ಅಪಾಯ ಕಡಿಮೆ ಮಾಡಲು ನಿಯಮಿತ ಏರೋಬಿಕ್ ವ್ಯಾಯಾಮ, ಆಂಟಿಆಕ್ಸಿಡೆಂಟ್ ಆಹಾರ, ಹಸಿರು ಚಹಾ, ಕೀಟನಾಶಕ/ರಸಾಯನಿಕ ಒಡ್ಡಿಗೆ ತಪ್ಪಿಸುವುದು, ತಲೆಗಾಯ ತಡೆಗಾಗಿ ಹೆಲ್ಮೆಟ್ ಧರಿಸುವುದು, ಮಾನಸಿಕ ಹಾಗೂ ಸಾಮಾಜಿಕ ಚಟುವಟಿಕೆಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಸಕ್ರಿಯವಾಗಿರುವುದು ಸಹಕಾರಿ. ನಿದ್ರೆ, ಸಕ್ಕರೆ, ರಕ್ತದೊತ್ತಡ ನಿಯಂತ್ರಣ ಕೂಡ ಮೆದುಳಿನ ಆರೋಗ್ಯಕ್ಕೆ ಒಳ್ಳೆಯದು. ಕುಟುಂಬ ಇತಿಹಾಸ ಇದ್ದವರು ಸಣ್ಣ ಲಕ್ಷಣಗಳಿಗೂ ಬೇಗ ತಪಾಸಣೆ ಮಾಡಿಸಬೇಕು.
kannada.Food: ಹೆಚ್ಚು ನಾರುಳ್ಳ ಆಹಾರ (ತರಕಾರಿ, ಹಣ್ಣು, ಧಾನ್ಯ, ಪಲ್ಸ್) ಮಲಬದ್ದತೆ ಕಡಿಮೆ ಮಾಡುತ್ತದೆ. ಸಾಕಷ್ಟು ನೀರು ಕುಡಿಯುವುದರಿಂದ ದೇಹದ ನೀರಿನ ಕೊರತೆ ಮತ್ತು ರಕ್ತದೊತ್ತಡ ಕುಸಿತ ಕಡಿಮೆ ಆಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಪ್ರೋಟೀನ್ ಅಗತ್ಯವಿದೆ, ಆದರೆ ಕೆಲವು ಔಷಧಿಗಳಿಗೆ ಊಟ ಸಮಯದ ಪ್ರೋಟೀನ್ ಹಂಚಿಕೆ ಅಗತ್ಯವಾಗಬಹುದು; ವೈದ್ಯರ ಸೂಚನೆ ಪಾಲಿಸಿ. ನುಂಗುವ ತೊಂದರೆ ಇದ್ದರೆ ಮೃದುವಾದ ಆಹಾರ ಬಳಸಿ. ಉಪ್ಪು ಮತ್ತು ಪ್ರಕ್ರಿಯೆಗೊಳಿಸಿದ ಆಹಾರ ಕಡಿಮೆ ಮಾಡಿ. ಸಮತೋಲನ ಆಹಾರ ದೇಹಶಕ್ತಿ ಮತ್ತು ಚಲನೆಗೆ ಸಹಾಯಕ.
kannada.Exercise: ಪ್ರತಿ ದಿನ 30 ನಿಮಿಷ ನಡೆಯುವುದು, ಸಮತೋಲನಕ್ಕೆ Tai Chi, ಸ್ನಾಯು ಬಲಕ್ಕೆ ಈಜು, ಸಂಯೋಜನೆಗೆ ನೃತ್ಯ, ಕಟ್ಟುತನಕ್ಕೆ ಸ್ಟ್ರೆಚಿಂಗ್, ಮಾತಿನ ಸ್ಪಷ್ಟತೆಗೆ ಸ್ಪೀಚ್ ಥೆರಪಿ ವ್ಯಾಯಾಮಗಳನ್ನು ಮಾಡಬೇಕು. ಜೊತೆಗೆ ಪೋಶ್ಚರ್ ಮತ್ತು ನಡೆ ಅಭ್ಯಾಸಗಳು ಬಿದ್ದುವ ಅಪಾಯ ಕಡಿಮೆ ಮಾಡುತ್ತವೆ. ಫಿಸಿಯೋಥೆರಪಿಸ್ಟ್ ಮಾರ್ಗದರ್ಶನದಲ್ಲಿ ಹಂತಕ್ಕೆ ತಕ್ಕ ವ್ಯಾಯಾಮ ಕ್ರಮ ರೂಪಿಸಬೇಕು. ನಿಯಮಿತ ಅಭ್ಯಾಸದಿಂದ ದೈನಂದಿನ ಕಾರ್ಯಕ್ಷಮತೆ ಸುಧಾರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.
kannada.How to control it?: ನರವೈದ್ಯರ ನಿಯಮಿತ ಫಾಲೋ-ಅಪ್, ಸಮಯಕ್ಕೆ ಔಷಧಿ ಸೇವನೆ, ಫಿಸಿಯೋಥೆರಪಿ, ಸ್ಪೀಚ್ ಮತ್ತು ನುಂಗುವ ತರಬೇತಿ, ಮನೆ ಸುರಕ್ಷತಾ ಬದಲಾವಣೆಗಳು ಮುಖ್ಯ ನಿಯಂತ್ರಣ ಕ್ರಮಗಳು. ಔಷಧಿ ಸಮಯ ತಪ್ಪಿದರೆ ಲಕ್ಷಣಗಳು ಅಚಾನಕ್ ಹೆಚ್ಚಬಹುದು. ಮಲಬದ್ದತೆ, ನಿದ್ರೆ ಸಮಸ್ಯೆ, ಭ್ರಮೆ, ಮನನೊಂದು ಮುಂತಾದ non-motor ಲಕ್ಷಣಗಳಿಗೂ ಚಿಕಿತ್ಸೆ ಅಗತ್ಯ. ಮನೆಯಲ್ಲಿನ ಬಿದ್ದುಕೊಳ್ಳುವ ಅಪಾಯದ ವಸ್ತುಗಳನ್ನು ತೆಗೆದುಹಾಕಿ. ಮುನ್ನಡೆದ ಹಂತದಲ್ಲಿ ವಿಶೇಷ ಕೇಂದ್ರಗಳಲ್ಲಿ advanced ಚಿಕಿತ್ಸೆ ಪರಿಗಣಿಸಬಹುದು.
kannada.When to see a doctor?: ವಿಶ್ರಾಂತಿ ಸಮಯದಲ್ಲಿ ಕೈ ನಡುಕು, ಕೈ/ಕಾಲುಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಕಟ್ಟುತನ, ದಿನನಿತ್ಯ ಕೆಲಸಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ನಿಧಾನ ಚಲನೆ, ಸಮತೋಲನ ಸಮಸ್ಯೆ ಮತ್ತು ಪದೇಪದೇ ಬೀಳುವುದು, ಸಣ್ಣ ಅಕ್ಷರದಲ್ಲಿ ಬರೆಯುವುದು, ಮೃದುವಾದ/ಅಸ್ಪಷ್ಟ ಮಾತು, ವಾಸನೆ ಅರಿವಿನ ಕುಸಿತ ಕಂಡರೆ ವೈದ್ಯರನ್ನು ಸಂಪರ್ಕಿಸಬೇಕು. ನುಂಗುವ ತೊಂದರೆ, ಗೊಂದಲ, ಔಷಧಿ ಪರಿಣಾಮ ಕಡಿಮೆ ಕಾಣುವುದು, ಹೆಚ್ಚುವರಿ ಬಿದ್ದುಕೊಳ್ಳುವಿಕೆ ಕಂಡರೂ ತಡ ಮಾಡಬಾರದು.
kannada.Emergency note: ಪಾರ್ಕಿನ್ಸನ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ ಕೆಲ ಸಂದರ್ಭಗಳು ತುರ್ತು: ನುಂಗಲು/ಉಸಿರಾಡಲು ಆಗದಿರುವುದು, ತೀವ್ರ ಗೊಂದಲ, ದೇಹ ಚಲನೆ ಸಂಪೂರ್ಣ ನಿಲ್ಲುವುದು, ಜ್ವರದೊಂದಿಗೆ ಕಟ್ಟುತನ, ತಲೆಗೆ ಗಾಯವಾಗುವಂತೆ ಬಿದ್ದುಕೊಳ್ಳುವುದು. ಇವು ಕಂಡರೆ ತಕ್ಷಣ ಆಸ್ಪತ್ರೆಗೆ ತೆರಳಬೇಕು.

hindi.What is the disease?: पार्किंसन रोग एक दीर्घकालिक तंत्रिका रोग है जिसमें मस्तिष्क की डोपामिन बनाने वाली कोशिकाएं धीरे-धीरे कम होती जाती हैं। डोपामिन कम होने से शरीर की चाल, संतुलन और गति प्रभावित होती है। मरीज में कंपकंपी, जकड़न, धीमी चाल और संतुलन समस्या विकसित होती है। यह रोग धीरे-धीरे बढ़ता है और कई साल चलता है। यह छूने से नहीं फैलता। पूर्ण इलाज अभी उपलब्ध नहीं है, लेकिन सही दवा, फिजियोथेरेपी, स्पीच थेरेपी और परिवार के सहयोग से लंबे समय तक लक्षण नियंत्रित रखे जा सकते हैं।
hindi.What are the symptoms?: आराम की अवस्था में हाथ कांपना, चलने में हाथ कम हिलना, काम में धीमापन, हाथ-पैर जकड़ना, धीमी या अस्पष्ट आवाज, छोटे अक्षर में लिखना, चेहरे की अभिव्यक्ति कम होना, नींद की परेशानी, कब्ज, सूंघने की क्षमता घटना जैसे लक्षण शुरू में दिख सकते हैं। आगे चलकर संतुलन बिगड़ना, बार-बार गिरना, चलना अचानक रुक जाना (freezing), निगलने में कठिनाई, भ्रम या याददाश्त की समस्या हो सकती है। सभी मरीजों में एक जैसे लक्षण नहीं होते, इसलिए विशेषज्ञ जांच जरूरी है।
hindi.What causes the disease?: सटीक कारण पूरी तरह ज्ञात नहीं है। मस्तिष्क के substantia nigra क्षेत्र में डोपामिन न्यूरॉन्स की क्षति मुख्य कारण मानी जाती है। उम्र बढ़ना, कुछ आनुवंशिक कारण, परिवार में इतिहास, कीटनाशक और रसायनों का संपर्क, तथा सिर की चोट जोखिम बढ़ा सकते हैं। अधिकतर मामलों में यह सीधे विरासत में नहीं आता। तनाव रोग का कारण नहीं, लेकिन लक्षण बढ़ा सकता है। शुरुआती चरण में न्यूरोलॉजिस्ट से जांच कराने से सही निदान और बेहतर उपचार योजना बनती है।
hindi.Stages: स्टेज 1: हल्के लक्षण शरीर के एक तरफ। स्टेज 2: दोनों तरफ लक्षण, संतुलन सामान्य। स्टेज 3: संतुलन प्रभावित, गिरने का जोखिम, फिर भी कुछ स्वतंत्रता। स्टेज 4: गंभीर लक्षण, दैनिक काम में मदद जरूरी। स्टेज 5: खड़ा/चल नहीं पाना, पूर्णकालिक देखभाल आवश्यक।
hindi.Prevention: No proven prevention but these reduce risk: Regular aerobic exercise, Green tea and antioxidant rich foods, Avoid exposure to pesticides and chemicals, Head injury prevention (wear helmets), Stay mentally and socially active. साथ ही नींद, रक्तचाप और शुगर नियंत्रण से मस्तिष्क स्वास्थ्य बेहतर रहता है। यह उपाय रोग को पूरी तरह रोकने की गारंटी नहीं देते, पर कार्यक्षमता बनाए रखने में मदद करते हैं। परिवार इतिहास वालों को शुरुआती लक्षण पर तुरंत जांच करानी चाहिए।
hindi.Food: फाइबर युक्त भोजन जैसे सब्जियां, फल, साबुत अनाज और दालें कब्ज कम करने में मदद करते हैं। पर्याप्त पानी जरूरी है ताकि निर्जलीकरण और चक्कर कम हों। प्रोटीन महत्वपूर्ण है, लेकिन कुछ मरीजों में दवा के साथ प्रोटीन समय का संतुलन आवश्यक होता है, इसलिए डॉक्टर की सलाह लें। निगलने में दिक्कत होने पर नरम भोजन और स्पीच-स्वैलो सलाह अपनाएं। बहुत ज्यादा प्रोसेस्ड, नमकीन और मीठे खाद्य पदार्थ सीमित रखें। संतुलित आहार से ताकत और दवा प्रतिक्रिया बेहतर होती है।
hindi.Exercise: Walking daily for 30 minutes, Tai Chi for balance improvement, Swimming for muscle strength, Dancing to improve coordination, Stretching exercises for stiffness, Speech therapy exercises बहुत उपयोगी हैं। इसके साथ posture training और gait practice से गिरने का जोखिम घटता है। शुरुआत में फिजियोथेरेपिस्ट की देखरेख में कार्यक्रम बनाएं। नियमितता सबसे महत्वपूर्ण है। उन्नत चरण में भी हल्की सहायक गतिविधि जकड़न कम करती है और दैनिक कार्यक्षमता बनाए रखती है।
hindi.How to control it?: नियंत्रण के लिए समय पर दवा, नियमित न्यूरोलॉजी फॉलो-अप, फिजियोथेरेपी, स्पीच/स्वैलो थेरेपी और घर में सुरक्षा बदलाव जरूरी हैं। दवा की खुराक छूटने पर अचानक जकड़न या चलने में रुकावट बढ़ सकती है। कब्ज, नींद, अवसाद, भ्रम जैसे non-motor लक्षणों का भी इलाज करें। घर में फिसलने वाले सामान हटाएं, सहारा रेलिंग लगाएं, और गिरने से बचाव करें। देखभाल करने वालों को प्रशिक्षण देना जरूरी है ताकि लक्षण उतार-चढ़ाव के समय सही मदद मिल सके।
hindi.When to see a doctor?: आराम में हाथ कांपना, हाथ-पैर में जकड़न, दैनिक काम में धीमी गति, संतुलन बिगड़ना और बार-बार गिरना, small handwriting (micrographia), soft or slurred speech, loss of smell जैसे लक्षण दिखें तो न्यूरोलॉजिस्ट से मिलें। निगलने में कठिनाई, बार-बार choking, भ्रम, या दवा का असर कम लगना भी चेतावनी है। जल्दी निदान से रोग नियंत्रण और स्वतंत्र जीवन अवधि बेहतर होती है।
hindi.Emergency note: यदि अचानक निगलना या सांस लेना मुश्किल हो, तेज भ्रम/हैलुसिनेशन हो, शरीर चलना बंद हो जाए, तेज बुखार के साथ जकड़न हो, या गिरकर सिर में चोट लगे तो तुरंत इमरजेंसी में जाएं। देर करना खतरनाक हो सकता है।
